However, Lucresia seemed as if she hadn’t heard the sailor’s loud warnings, staring with a strange gaze at the Brilliant Starship gradually approaching through the fog. Then, as if struck by a sudden thought, she sharply turned, scanning her surroundings.
The phantom image of Homeloss overlaid this ship, with the color of the dark wooden deck surfacing translucent Spiritual Fires and ghostly Spiritual Bodies’ sails hanging high on the mast—everything precisely as she vividly remembered.
In this final voyage at the world’s end, she finally unraveled the mystery that had long baffled even her "father."
It was she herself, who had guided her own course...
"Don’t worry," she finally spoke softly, her voice faint but causing an instant hush on deck, "We won’t meet that ship—we will just pass by each other. Maintain our current course, passing by its side without any interaction."
"Alright... as long as the ’you’ on that ship doesn’t suddenly come close," the sailor muttered, not questioning the "captain’s" judgment at the moment, but following the order to steer his spatially ’hybrid’ ship slowly past the side of that Brilliant Starship.
Everyone tensed up at this moment, watching the Brilliant Starship from another timeline emerge from the fog, drawing closer until its many details could be distinguished. They noticed many differences from their own recollection of the ship, seemingly because it was a version from decades ago; observing the ship’s brief deceleration and attitude adjustment, apparently a momentary panic and unsteadiness due to the sudden proximity of Homeloss, but finally, both ships passed each other without incident.
Lucresia breathed a slight sigh of relief.
Then, within a few seconds after the two ships completely passed each other, that Brilliant Starship from another timeline swiftly dissolved, vanishing like a phantom into the fog.
The convergence of time flows has ended.
And this was exactly what Lucresia was waiting for—she immediately ordered, "Turn the bow around, follow the last disappearance trajectory of that ship, that’s the direction back to the Endless Sea."
The sailor hesitated for a moment in his heart but carried out the captain’s order without delay. After the ship beneath his feet slowly adjusted its course, he then twisted his head to look at the "Sea Witch" and said, "Ma’am, are you...?"
"This has happened before, decades ago. The Brilliant Starship once encountered the ’phantom’ of Homeloss beyond the critical line of Six Nautical Miles. I still remember the details from that time," Lucresia nodded, "Don’t think too much now, first think of a way to get out of here."
"It’s better not to overthink. My head is about to burst," Sherry scratched her head, obviously a bit confused after quickly sorting things out in her mind, "So, decades ago on the border you met a guiding phantom, which actually was you from decades later, but your future self was also lost—neither of the ships knew the way back, yet they both eventually found the correct direction... What is even going on..."
"Causality, luck, space-time, everything here is a mess," Morris said with a pipe in his mouth that seemed rarely truly lit, his voice sounding somewhat muted, "Don’t use too much rational thinking in the border seas. Human minds have a limit when bearing ’irrationality.’ Don’t let those irrational elements drive you mad."
No sooner had the old man finished speaking than Dog by his side murmured in a muted voice, "Sherry is fine, she doesn’t think much normally, her mind is as fresh as new."
Sherry immediately punched Dog on the head, making a "clang" sound.
Lucresia didn’t pay attention to the commotion beside her, neither did the helmsman—they were still intently staring ahead along the navigational route, in the direction pointed by the bow of the Brilliant Starship, where the thick fog seemed to be undergoing some changes.
Nina suddenly realized that the Brilliant Starship was gradually slowing down.
She looked up in surprise, "Eh? Miss Lucresia, why are we slowing down now?"
"...There’s a ’critical change’ in the fog ahead, that should be the place across the critical line of Six Nautical Miles. Passing through that boundary, we enter the relatively safe waters of the Veil Sea," Lucresia spoke slowly, but then her tone deepened, "But there’s a problem."
Nina looked puzzled, and the helmsman, who obviously had understood, tugged at the corner of his mouth, producing a hoarse and ugly voice, "Once we ’cross the boundary’ at that spot, the date of our return to the Endless Sea is fixed—but it might not necessarily be a day in 1902."
Nina puzzled for less than a few seconds before slowly widening her eyes, as clever as she was, she instantly understood the meaning behind the sailor’s words.
"We exited the ’channel’ ahead of time, and at that moment of departure from our course, the time flows around us probably got messed up," Lucresia said solemnly, "And just now, the Brilliant Starship from decades ago appeared in our sight, that might be the shadow of another time flow that strayed into our course, but it could also be us ’entering’ the wrong time flow..."
This time even Sherry, who was nearby, understood and was instantly shocked: "Does that mean, if we go back now, we might end up decades ago?!"
The sailor sighed, "That would actually be one of the better scenarios—if it’s worse, the flow of time has completely jumbled, and after crossing the boundary, we could enter any point in time."
Sherry: "...Fuck..."
"Should we contact the captain?" Fenna suddenly said, "This is already beyond our plan, perhaps the captain’s power can..."
"No, I’ve tried just now, but I could only vaguely sense my father’s voice," Lucresia shook her head, "We are still in the chaotic streams of the border, the chaotic temporal order here is causing interference, and over there at my father’s side..."
She paused for a moment and gently shook her head.
The people on the deck looked at each other.
The Brilliant Starship cruised at an extremely low speed near that "critical line" in the mist, slowly sailing in a position that was relatively "safe" and wasn’t going to plunge into "deeper dangers".
The way home was right in front of them, as if one could step over it just by stretching out a leg—there was nothing blocking, no impediments at all.
However, standing in front of the Brilliant Starship was a barrier far more dangerous than any wall or trench—time.
On the bridge, the automaton Luny was monitoring the incredibly complex systems of the Brilliant Starship, while the rabbit Rabi carefully nestled in the corner, holding the little doll Niru and not daring to breathe, and Agatha’s figure hazily reflected in a nearby porthole, with others sitting around the captain’s seat in a rather oppressive atmosphere.
Morris muttered, "It would be nice if there was a ’guiding anchor’ from the Endless Sea, even a piece of wood that drifted past the curtain would do."
"The probability of that isn’t better than us crossing the border and accurately arriving in the year 1902," Lucresia shook her head, "this is the border after all."
Sherry scratched her head, muttering, "If we really ended up decades ago, even hundreds or thousands of years ago..."
She muttered a few words, then didn’t continue.
But Fenna quietly repeated the words Sherry said, "Hundreds of years...."
"Then we would have arrived ’too early’," Nina stuck out her tongue, "The good news is that we could see the ’sun’ that was still normal back then."
Fenna did not respond to Nina’s words but suddenly looked up at Lucresia, her expression very serious: "Miss Lucresia, how long can you live?"
The scene suddenly grew quiet, Lucresia understood what Fenna meant, and after a brief pondering, she broke the silence: "I’m not sure how long this ’curse’ can last, but at least... a few hundred years should be no problem."
Morris then shook his head, "My lifespan is limited, even with the blessing of machinery and wisdom, this body will wear out."
Agatha’s voice came from the side: "In theory, I have no lifespan limits, but lacking a physical medium, my existence is not stable..."
"Profound Demons can live for a long time," Fenna suddenly looked at Sherry, "At least, I haven’t heard of any Profound Demon that ’died of old age’ because they reached the limit of their life, as long as you hide well, avoid being discovered by the church guardians of the current era..."
Sherry listened dumbfoundedly, gradually coming to a realization: "Ah... you can’t be serious..."
"We need to prepare for the worst-case scenario," Fenna said seriously.
"Then let’s think about an even worse situation," Lucresia suddenly shook her head, "What if we didn’t arrive too early, but ’too late’? When father needs us, we might not have arrived yet..."
Everyone suddenly fell silent.
Quietness and oppressiveness once again enveloped the bridge.
But just then, there was a sudden buzz from the direction of the control console.
Following that, the automaton Luny who was monitoring the devices exclaimed:
"Mistress, there’s a signal!"

chapters.title: Chapter 834 - 831: The Silent Call
chapters.content:
Chapter 834: Chapter 831: The Silent Call
A signal!
Silence fell on the bridge in an instant, even the usually cool and calm Lukelecia widened her eyes slightly—a "signal" had appeared in this "beyond the border," past the Six Nautical Miles critical line. It would be difficult for anyone to maintain their composure, let alone in this situation where they were already lost at sea!
How could there be a signal in this place? Who sent it? Was it a real "event," or... another treacherous trap created by the thick fog for unwelcome visitors?
"Prepare for protection!" Lukelecia spoke instantly, her figure flashed to the control panel side, and at the same time, she pulled a lever between the devices. Luny at her side also reacted immediately, the automaton rapidly pressed several buttons on the platform, then stepped back, pulling out the winding key on her back slightly and turning it three full circles in reverse.
Accompanied by a slight clicking sound, Luny’s arms, legs, and neck suddenly cracked open with delicate seams, and runes began to light up under her skin, her eyes starting to emit a faint dark red glow. At the same time, sounds of mechanical operations came from all over the bridge, many previously concealed grilles and duct outlets flipped out from the floor and walls, and the scent of incense and a strange deep humming sound enveloped everyone.
Sherry stared dumbfounded at this scene, and only after a moment did she let out a surprised exclamation: "...Wow... you actually have such an impressive thing?!"
Nina also couldn’t help but be dumbstruck, staring with wide eyes at the automaton now in some kind of defensive stance: "...How did you just change?"
Luny, rattled by Nina’s burning gaze (perhaps literally), trembled as a sound of colliding parts came from within: "The mistress doesn’t let others dismantle me..."
"It’s always necessary to be prepared for unexpected situations when exploring the frontier year-round," Lukelecia sighed lightly, glancing at Profound Demons and Sun Shard who seemed to have no sense of crisis, "Stay alert, I’m going to connect to the signal now—what’s on the other end of the radio might not be human voices, or even ’voices’ at all... Never mind, you guys probably aren’t scared of it."
As she finished speaking, she took a deep breath and placed her hand on the communication device—click.
A broken voice mixed with severe static, as if it had passed through countless levels of interference and distortion, came out from the speaker: "...Calling...zzzt...this is...zzzt...the Lighthouse, calling...Voyager, waiting for your...zzzt...return. Repeat, this is...zzzt..."
The hoarse and monotonous calling seemed to echo through the crevices of time and space, repeating over and over like a ghost.
Everyone on the bridge was stunned, even Lukelecia appeared astonished.
"The Lighthouse?" After a long while, Sherry muttered to herself, then suddenly jolted as if she recalled something, "Wait, I remember now! When we set off, the last stop..."
Lukelecia suddenly recalled the words spoken by the Female Pope at the last frontier mobile port of the Deep Sea Church, before the fleet had crossed the curtain—
"Three warships will stay near the Lighthouse, waiting for your return... This mobile port will remain here, and my avatar will stay as well, until you come back..."
"...The Lighthouse is still there, and they’re actually still waiting?!" Sherry’s eyes widened; she might not be the best at academics, but her memory was always sharp, "The whole world has almost come to a halt!"
Lukelecia did not speak; although she remembered the situation at departure, she still didn’t let the excitement affect her calmness—she first confirmed that the signal did not contain traces of distortion or tampering, and that it wasn’t a collective hallucination of the crew on the bridge "reflected" by the mental impact from the border sea, then she confirmed the Brilliant Starship’s defensive situation before picking up the microphone from the communications desk and placing it to her mouth: "Voyager received, this is the Brilliant Starship, we are attempting to return from the critical line, navigation on the ship has failed, please boost the Lighthouse’s antenna power."
She put down the microphone, waiting patiently.
However, static noises from the communication device followed, and a few seconds later, the repetitive monotone content remained: "This is...zzzt...The Lighthouse, calling...Voyager...zzzt..."
Lukelecia’s brow furrowed gradually, her expression becoming serious as she attempted to make contact again, but still no reply came from the other side; even worse, after another repetition, not even the voice could be heard anymore, only the interference-like zzzt sound remained.
"They can’t hear us?" Nina asked curiously, widening her eyes, "Is it being interfered with?"
"Don’t know, but we can be sure the signal is indeed coming from ’The Lighthouse,’" Lukelecia said with her brows deeply furrowed and at the same time looked towards Luny, "Can you track the direction the signal is coming from?"
"The strength isn’t enough, but a general direction can be tracked," Luny quickly responded while operating the equipment beside her, "Are we going in this direction?"
Lukelecia turned her head back, glancing in the direction of Morris.
After exchanging glances, both nodded lightly.
This was the "guiding anchor point" for returning home—the piece of "wood" that drifted from the other side of the border.
"We will at least make it back to around the year 1902," Lukelecia murmured to herself softly.
The Brilliant Starship slowly adjusted its course; after patrolling the Six Nautical Miles critical line for a long while and enhancing the antenna’s sensitivity as much as possible to determine the direction of the signal, it finally found a most likely "gap" within that border line.
Then the ship’s horn sounded, with a resolute determination to move forward, this vessel—covered with the phantom of Homeloss, the Voyager that had drifted at the end of the world for so long—plunged into the fog of returning home.
As they crossed that critical line, the crew hardly felt anything, only Luc Recia, who had spent years exploring the border waters, could faintly perceive the indescribable "change".
Her expression was tense, her senses highly alert, picking up on everything around her, paying close attention to the signals from the communication device—
Have we returned? Have we returned to around the year 1902?
Fortunately, fate did not continue to play tricks on those journeying home; almost the instant the boundary was crossed, Luny excitedly reported: "Mistress, the signal has significantly strengthened—we have successfully returned within the veil, and we also received the time-setting signal just now, our timing is accurate!"
Luc Recia finally let out a sigh of relief—the last time she felt this kind of deep-seated relaxation and joy was when her brother had contacted her and told her "Father has indeed regained his humanity".
Sherry and Nina’s cheers, along with Rabi’s finally daring to breathe in the corner and Niru the little puppet’s quiet cheers, filled the bridge.
"Continue moving towards the signal," Luc Recia ordered, then picked up the handset of the communication device once more, calling out to the lighthouse again, "This is Brilliant Starship, we have successfully crossed the critical line, moving towards the lighthouse, how are you doing over there?"
However, after calling out twice in a row, there was still only the rustling noise of static in the communication device—although the signal had already strengthened to a degree that should not affect communications, the lighthouse still gave no response.
It was as if that previous call for the return journey... was just an illusion.
Luc Recia’s expression gradually grew solemn again, and the bridge, which had just relaxed for a moment, once again became somewhat serious.
Luc Recia put down the handset, shook her head, and said: "...Something seems off with the lighthouse; we’ll head over there first and see."
The "lighthouse", standing in the depths of the border’s dense mist near the Six Nautical Miles critical line, capable of penetrating the signal through the critical line to a certain extent, finally came into view of Brilliant Starship.
It was still lit, with its blessed light shimmering, seemingly fainter than when they set off, but still piercing through the thick fog.
Upon seeing that light, everyone relaxed a bit—with the signal there and the light still on, at the very least it indicated that the lighthouse had been maintained recently.
But why was it so silent?
After an especially long journey, Brilliant Starship finally arrived near the lighthouse.
At first glance, Luc Recia saw those three colossal Deep Sea Church warships still quietly docked at the port of the mobile platform beneath the lighthouse, with various lights on the side of the ships still lit, clearly still operating normally—yet there was no sign of response as Brilliant Starship approached.
It was as if, although there were people maintaining the ships’ facilities, no one reacted to the return of the Voyager.
"I think I just saw a shadow moving on the upper level of the lighthouse," Sherry said in a low voice, coming onto the deck and looking up at the distance, "There are people up there, but it seems like no one is paying attention to us... Can they not see us?"
"Could all of this actually be an illusion...?" Nina worriedly muttered.
"...What if we are the illusions?" Sherry muttered more frighteningly.
Luc Recia ignored the two girls scaring each other with their whispers; she had also noticed that there indeed seemed to be people moving within the lighthouse facilities. After weighing the options briefly, she quickly made a decision:
"Fenna and I will go up to investigate. Everyone else stay on the ship. Do not leave the ship before we return, and do not trust any voices that appear on the communicator or any approaching figures. Luny, take care of the ship."
Luny immediately bowed slightly: "Yes, Mistress."
After making quick preparations, Luc Recia and Fenna quietly boarded the origami boat and stealthily ascended the strangely silent lighthouse.
The surroundings were very quiet, the cold wind blowing through the harbor, carrying a kind of "cold" that seemed to permeate flesh and blood, numbing the heart and vessels gradually.
Luc Recia and Fenna stepped onto the dock’s pier, looking around in the darkness and the fog.
There were many shadows, moving within the mist.
Yet no one paid any attention to them.

chapters.title: Chapter 835 - 832: Returning Home, From Afar
chapters.content:
Chapter 835: Chapter 832: Returning Home, From Afar
Lucresia and Fenna walked on the mechanical platform beneath the lighthouse facility, passing through the dense fog in the night, walking along those familiar paths and corridors. The dim yellow lights in the mist seemed like obscure stars, and within those dim and indistinct shadows, someone was moving around near them.
A pale-faced harbor guard walked past Fenna, donned in a crisp uniform, holding a lantern that was still bright in his hand. His expression was meticulous, but when two uninvited guests appeared before him, he simply ignored them as if they were invisible.
With a complex gaze, Fenna watched the guard recede into the fog. After his silhouette gradually vanished, she whispered to Lucresia, "...he wasn’t breathing."
"Yes, the person before him wasn’t either; most people here no longer breathe," Lucresia replied softly, her face shrouded in shadows, "Even the few who still breathe don’t react to our arrival."
"Everyone seems to be in a state of..." Fenna began, but then stumbled over her words, finding it hard to come up with the right term to describe her feelings. After a long pause, she continued, "A state of confusion and ’ignorance’, they still maintain their daily routines, even performing thorough handovers at each post, but they simply don’t react to us."
Lucresia hummed softly but said nothing more. Instead, she estimated the distribution of the facilities in the fog and started walking towards the church at the base of the lighthouse.
The situation inside the church was not much different from the outside, only with fewer people. Aside from a few figures resting and praying, there was only a priestess in a black nun’s robe cleaning the main hall. She seemed to have a slight reaction to the appearance of Fenna and Lucresia—a brief pause and gaze—but when Fenna was just about to speak to the nun, the latter casually walked away.
Lucresia and Fenna went straight through the main hall of the church and entered the tower connected to the lighthouse from a side door, then ascended the misty spiral staircase, searching several empty rest and storage rooms until they found a slightly ajar door.
Bright light and a faint buzzing noise came from behind the door.
Fenna stepped forward to push the ajar door open and saw a small room filled with various devices. The scent of incense lingered in the room, where a small brass incense burner hung from a central steam pipe, looking as if it had been recently lit.
The two walked around the steam pipe, and almost at the same moment, a figure suddenly stood up from a corner of the room and headed straight towards Lucresia.
Lucresia was startled by the figure that had been sitting in the corner all along. Only then did she notice it was a middle-aged man cloaked in a priest’s robe—he had no breath or heartbeat; indeed, no "presence" at all. He sat there like a mere "object," so much so that even Fenna failed to realize there was another person in the room!
Then, the middle-aged priest without any sign of life emotionlessly bypassed Lucresia and Fenna. In their bewildered gaze, he sat down at a table at the end of the room, cleared his throat like a machine reaching its designated position on a timer, and pressed a button on the table, bringing a microphone in front of him.
"Calling Homeloss, calling Brilliant Starship, this is the Border Lighthouse. The current time is December 17, 1902, we are waiting for your return... repeat, calling Voyagers, this is the Border Lighthouse, the current time is... we are waiting for your return..."
The middle-aged priest repeated it three times, then waited a while, pressed the button again, and repeated the message. After several times, he switched the equipment to listen mode, stood up from the table, and walked back to his previous spot.
He walked past Lucresia and Fenna, without casting a glance.
"That was the call we heard." Fenna watched the scene in a daze before speaking softly after a long while. She turned to the "witch" beside her, only to find that the latter was also looking up at her.
"I’ve heard my father describe the current state of the Endless Sea, but I never fully pictured what it would actually look like," Lucresia said with a complex tone, "This is even more... more..."
She repeated herself several times but ultimately could not find the right words to express her feelings.
"...The situation inside the City-State shouldn’t be this bad," Fenna gently shook her head after a moment of thought, "This lighthouse is located in the deepest part of the border; order here faded earliest, and this place is also more susceptible to the corruption of the gods. On the other side in the City-State..."
"Yes, the situation will be somewhat better, though it may deteriorate later," Lucresia interjected seriously, "Let’s not think too much about it now."
"...Right, let’s not think too much about it now." Fenna was momentarily startled by the response before quickly regaining her composure, pushing aside the associations and worries in her heart. Then, she heard footsteps approaching from outside the door.
The two instinctively turned around, and almost at the same time, the slightly ajar door was pushed open by someone from the outside—a man in a guard’s uniform appeared at the door.
Perhaps he was looking for the middle-aged priest.
Fenna, now accustomed to the "environment" here, thought so, stepping aside to give way, but as she did so, a look of astonishment appeared on the black-garbed guard’s face—he seemed to have suddenly noticed the two ladies in the room, his body shook slightly, and excitement and joy appeared in his eyes.
"Lady Fenna, and Miss Lucresia!" The guard exclaimed with excitement, rubbing his eyes in disbelief, "Is it really you? Have you come back?!"
Frankly, Fenna was even more stunned than the guard in that instant, remaining frozen for two seconds before her eyes suddenly widened: "You’re still ’awake’?!"
"Awake?" The black-clothed guard was briefly startled, but quickly understood the implication. He lowered his head to look at himself, then glanced at his resting compatriot in the corner of the room, a complex smile surfacing on his face, "Yes, I am awake. And there are others who are awake too. Everyone will be very happy to see you..."
"Others ’awake’ as well?" Lucresia was greatly surprised, "On our way here..."
"Those who are awake are few and far between. To facilitate looking out for each other and confirming our statuses, we all gather in the internal living area beneath the lighthouse. We only venture out to patrol the sectors when necessary, to resupply, and to check for other awakened brethren in need of assistance," the guard spoke calmly, "Additionally... it is to confirm whether you have returned."
He paused, then lifted his head to look at the middle-aged priest sitting in the corner of the room.
"The communication devices are now occupied by ’them.’ Forcibly disrupting their side’s ’daily activities’ can provoke rather intense reactions. Sometimes it can even trigger mayhem, so we only send someone up during specific ’window periods’ each day to check the listening antenna’s records, as well as to ascend to the top of the lighthouse to confirm whether there are ships returning from deep within the dense fog. Today it is my turn. But to be honest..."
The guardian let out a bittersweet smile, his eyes brimming with joy: "To be honest, I never really thought I would see you appear.
"I gaze out at that dense fog every day, but there is nothing but fog.
"Have all of you returned? What is the situation at the edge of the world like?"
Fenna and Lucresia exchanged glances, the latter hesitated briefly before nodding slightly, "The current situation is complicated, and it will take a long time to explain. Take us to your ’Shelter’ first."
"Of course," the black-clothed guard immediately nodded, "But before entering the Shelter, you need to undergo a ritual check—I hope you understand, this is after all the frontier, and you are returning from the dense fog.
"After that, an avatar of Helena will personally receive you."
Upon hearing this, Fenna instantly revealed a look of surprise: "The Pope’s avatar is here?"
"She was originally stationed at the mobile port that lies at the boundary between the Eternal Veil and the Endless Sea, but she came here after the situation at the lighthouse deteriorated. The Shelter is also maintained thanks to her—she has always been with us."
The black-clothed guard said this, then made an inviting gesture and turned to lead Fenna and Lucresia toward the door.
When they reached the entrance, he suddenly stopped, turned around, and looked at the two Voyagers who had just returned from the edge of the world.
Joy and excitement gradually settled in his eyes, finally transforming into a smile.
"Although the ’home’ situation isn’t so good right now..." he said solemnly, "welcome home—thank you for your efforts on the journey."
Fenna responded with a smile: "Yes, we’ve come back."
...
They had come home; though there were some complications, those who had sailed back eventually arrived safely at the port of return.
Only after receiving a message from Lucresia did Duncan finally relax.
He and Alice remained on the "Ceremonial Island" where the Queen Leviathan slumbered, having spent several days on this black island.
Now, the island was burning amidst flames that seemed like nebulae illusions, diffusing starlight.
The "flames" that resembled sprays of light from a nascent nebula spread across the entire black island, seeping out of every crack in the rocks, every block of stone, every pillar and rooftop joint, immersing everything here and even spreading to the sea around, reaching the carcasses of the Leviathan Beasts that were like archipelagos.
Duncan sat on a large stone at the edge of the plaza in front of the dark temple, calmly watching the flames burn, watching it permeate the "foundation stone" of this world.
The doll Eli stood quietly behind him.

chapters.title: Chapter 836 - 833 Their Last Journey
chapters.content:
Chapter 836: Chapter 833 Their Last Journey
The "flames" among the stars flowed at the end of this world, and in Duncan Zhouming’s perception, he felt as if he could clearly see those sparks slowly connecting into a ring—
Every ember he had left at the four nodes of the external barrier was now evenly spreading out its starlight, and at this moment, this light was progressively penetrating, covering those nodes – covering the "ancient gods" that constituted the nodes, covering their authority, covering their essence, covering their memories, covering... their information.
Just like the first time he penetrated the golden sun mask with his flame and glimpsed the secrets hidden behind it, just like how he usually probed and controlled those Transcendent items with his flame, what he was doing now was, in fact, still the same thing.
Every piece of data from the inception to the end of this world was gradually entering his mind during this process.
Because in the eyes of the "Reverse Singularity," this entire Endless Sea, this pile of ashes that was cooling down yet stubbornly pretending to have a breath of civilization left, was in itself a "Transcendent item."
Alice lowered her head, curiously looking at Duncan: "Captain, how much longer do we have to wait here?"
"We can leave now," Duncan said softly, "Nina and the others have safely returned to the Endless Sea, and now it’s time for us to continue to the next place."
Alice was curious: "The next place? You haven’t told me where it is yet..."
"We have to find it ourselves — but it shouldn’t be hard," said Duncan slowly, then lowered his head to look at an object lying next to him.
It was an ancient and delicate hourglass, the "life force" that the death god Bartok left for the Storm Goddess Gomona, and Duncan had taken this hourglass from the temple three days ago.
Now, the sand in the hourglass representing life was about to run out.
Duncan picked up the hourglass, and a flame was burning ethereally and quietly inside its vessel. The last few grains of sand did not fall but floated in the center of the container within the flame. He watched the last of the "life force," hearing faint and slight sounds from within, then gently nodded: "Yes, I am about to leave."
The faint voices seemed to be bidding him farewell, but almost nothing could be clearly heard.
Yet Duncan seemed to have understood all of it, he started to smile, his tone filled with warmth and delight: "Ah, that sounds nice... wanting to be with friends again, wanting to travel, to have a lively troupe... and then also wanting to open a souvenir shop?
"Good, I understand, I will arrange it... no need for doubts and worries, it will happen, this is the one and only chance to customize your world and future — you all deserve this opportunity.
"...Yes, it will take some time, an extremely long time, but there’s no need to worry, time is what I have most in abundance, to eternity, it only takes a blink of an eye...
"Now, we must go, Gomona, farewell — have sweet dreams."
The last grain of sand silently disintegrated in the flame, the hourglass quietly crumbled into dust, which scattered in the wind, and the entire island began to sink bit by bit into the starlight-filled flames.
Duncan stood up, waving his hand to open the fiery gateway to the Homeloss.
A moment later, they had returned to the Homeloss—under the control of the goat-headed figure, the ship was gliding smoothly through the fog between the Leviathan Islands, approaching the edge of the node sea.
Duncan took Alice to the captain’s quarters. The moment the door opened, the goat-headed figure, who had been daydreaming at the edge of the sea-chart table, immediately turned its head. The dutiful first officer quickly let out a long sigh, taking advantage of the captain’s silence to start babbling:
"Ah, it really feels unusual for the ship to be so quiet — usually at this time, Miss Fenna should have started exercising on the deck, and Sherry definitely would be ’adventuring’ all over with A-Dog. I initially thought they were too noisy and wished for some peace and quiet. Who knew this would suddenly become so quiet that it feels so uncomfortable — it’s just like returning to the state when we first came aboard. Thinking back, time really does fly. You know, human hearts are such curious things. How could I not have imagined going through all these experiences? And of course, now I can’t really be said to have a human heart, all right I’m done, I’ll shut up."
The goat-headed figure promptly shut its mouth by itself, not even giving Duncan the chance to tell it to "shut up"—the latter felt like he was being steamrolled by an unending barrage of words as solid as a wall and was about to tell the blabbermouth to zip it when, unexpectedly, it anticipated the response, leaving Duncan with nothing to say, just staring at the table’s wooden carving, uttering after a while, "You can shut up on your own?"
The goat-headed was expressionless (not that its stiff face ever showed much emotion), "Of course, once I’ve finished speaking, that’s it."
Duncan was choked up once more, suspecting the creature did it on purpose, and the evidence was ample, but the goat-headed figure surely didn’t care about that, so he just had to keep a straight face: "...Then you keep on shutting up here, Alice and I are going to deal with the next navigation issue."
The goat-headed figure was succinct: "Understood."
Duncan’s mouth twitched, leading the doll towards the bedroom in the depths of the captain’s quarters. Approaching the door, he couldn’t help but murmur to Alice: "Later, I’ll note to add a rule to the new world — anyone who speaks without punctuation will taste their own tongue..."
Alice also leaned in and whispered: "But Mr. Goat-Head doesn’t have a tongue at all, its voice comes directly from its neck..."
Duncan entered the room, casually closing the door behind him, and turned his head to look at Miss Doll upon hearing that: "Now that you mention it, I’m curious, do you have a tongue?"
"I do," Alice said seriously, opening her mouth and tugging at her cheek with her finger, "Look — prrt, a tongue."
"...I’m really curious how that error replication of Navigator One originally ’created’ you, they even made a tongue but couldn’t reinforce the joints." Duncan gave the adorable doll a somewhat curious glance, turned toward the bed, and took out the winding key that activated "Alice’s Mansion for Navigators," then dangled it in front of the doll.
Without the captain’s order, Alice already sat down in front of Duncan, skillfully turned around, unzipped her back, and exposed the keyhole.
Duncan picked up the navigator’s key, but before winding the spring, he suddenly fell silent while looking at Alice’s back, and then after a moment he spoke up, "Alice, I have a question."
"Hmm? Go ahead."
"Have you ever thought about... wanting something? Such as desires or wishes, for instance... not to continue being an ’automaton’?"
While adjusting her clothes, Alice turned her head with some confusion, "No, is there something wrong with being an automaton?"
"Don’t you have any demands or thoughts about the new world and the future?" Duncan asked seriously, "On this matter, Nina and the others all have more or less their own ideas, Sherry wants a big open space of her own, Morris wants room for research and exploration, even the Leviathan Queen has her own wishes she wants to fulfill, but you... you’ve always been quiet, and when we discuss the new world, you’ve never expressed an opinion."
Alice paused, seemingly contemplating the captain’s question carefully, but after a while, she shook her head, "Because I really don’t have any particular opinions."
Duncan slightly furrowed his brow.
"Because there’s nothing I’m dissatisfied with; everything is good," Alice said earnestly, "And I don’t know what the new world should be like. Everything I’ve seen since the day I ’awoke’ is here, and having these is enough, nothing more... Besides, it’s quite nice to be an automaton, I like it as it is now."
Upon saying this, she suddenly paused, then quickly added, "Ah, if I had to say something, then in the new world I would still want to stay with you—I can’t get accustomed to living in the City-State."
Duncan paused, finally a mix of surprise and consternation melted into a reluctant and gentle smile on his face.
"Alright," he nodded gently, reached out to pat Alice’s hair, "I will take you with me, but that’s just the fundamental—If you really don’t know what you want, leave it to me, I’ll help you figure it out and make it happen."
"Oh, okay!" Alice nodded happily, moving on the berth to turn around, but suddenly seemed to recall something, twisting her head in delight, "Ah right, I want a new frying pan, a smaller one, the kind that can be used to make tiny sweet pancakes, please add that to the list."
"...Alright, I’ve noted it down," Duncan paused, a gentle smile gradually appearing on his face, nodding solemnly, "In the new world, Alice wants a new frying pan."
"The kind used to make tiny sweet pancakes!"
"Yes, the kind used to make tiny sweet pancakes."
As the key slid into the lock, accompanied by a click, the key turned automatically within the automaton’s keyhole—the transitioning of lights and shadows, the resetting of senses, Duncan opened his eyes, only to find himself back at the place he left before leaving Alice’s Mansion.
The main hall of Navigator Three.
Dim lights spilled from high above, and in the center of the dark hall stood a "tree" woven of cables, pipelines, and metallic branches. On the edge of the platform where its roots were, an automaton cradling a drawing board was slowly opening her eyes—like a robot gradually booting up after being powered on, she slowly came to awaken, then her face lit up with a smile.
"Captain! We’ve entered again!"
Duncan nodded, walked over, and helped the automaton, who felt a bit unsteady from just waking up, to her feet.
"Captain, what do we do next? Should we greet the Black Sun at the door? Should we look for the... next course you spoke of?"
Duncan looked down at the "drawing board" in Alice’s hands.
This so-called "drawing board" was essentially Navigator Three’s remaining "functional interface".
"I want you to search for something." he stated.
"Search for something? What am I searching for?"
"The New Hope’s escape pod—it’s lost at the end of the ashes."
(It’s time to promote a book, the new novel by Toad "The First Magic World War"—
Charlotte McAllen travels to the Fals Empire, wanting to be a civil servant on a different continent; she’s not a combatant... But who would have expected that even civil servants have to go to the battlefield!)
Plugging a book at the completion of this one, nurturing and then leave fate to chance afterwards...)

chapters.title: Chapter 837 - 834 The True Appearance of the Mansion
chapters.content:
Chapter 837: Chapter 834 The True Appearance of the Mansion
Hearing the captain’s orders, Alice immediately began to think very seriously—then looked even more seriously into Duncan’s eyes: "What is an escape pod?"
Duncan wasn’t surprised by this at all, he would actually start to worry the day this doll lady stopped malfunctioning—however, the situation at hand isn’t too problematic, because after several incidents, he had confirmed that "Alice" might be clueless about many things, but the operational state of "Navigation System Three" was actually still pretty much online, and that old yet powerful spatial navigation system... was within Alice’s "instincts".
Now all that was needed was to make Alice’s "instinct" realize that a part of this mansion was missing—theoretically, that is.
"It’s a part that’s missing from this ’Alice’s Mansion’, but you don’t have to understand exactly what it is," seeing the doll still staring at him curiously with wide eyes, Duncan said casually, "Do you remember what I told you about the Frost Queen?"
Alice thought for a while: "Which one? There are many, but I don’t seem to remember all of them..."
"Lei Nora took a room from your ’mansion’, that room, is what I call the escape pod, and now she has ’ridden’ the escape pod to the ashen lands at the edge of the world. I need to pinpoint her location," Duncan explained patiently, "It’s okay if you don’t understand now, I will try to guide you through the process of ’understanding’ it."
Alice listened as if she understood, but still nodded quickly after the captain finished speaking: "Oh, what do I need to do now?"
"You stay here, keep sitting under this ’tree’, just like you did when you analyzed the external barrier’s navigation route, maintain the ’connection’ with this mansion," as Duncan spoke, he lifted his right hand, and a cluster of soft green flame, imbued with starlight, quietly burned in his palm, he handed this flame to the doll before him, "Take this, it will establish an additional ’bridge’ between you and me, I’m going to the ’damaged’ part of the mansion to make markings. If things are as I predict, I should be able to ’intervene’ in the operation of Navigation System Three through this method, bridging externally to transfer data into your ’system core’."
Alice uttered "oh", immediately nodded happily and agreed: "Mhm, okay!"
As she spoke, she reached out without hesitation to grasp the cluster of flame handed to her by the captain—a strange warmth touched her palm, the ethereal flame seemingly gaining tangibility, gently swaying in her hand.
Alice carefully cradled the small flame, with her other hand clutching her "tablet", turned around and returned to the side of the "Data Tree" woven from countless cables and pipes, and sat down on the platform, lifting her head with a radiant smile: "I’m ready!"
Duncan smiled and nodded his head, then turned and left the hall—he passed through the ornate door that originally connected the garden and the depths of the mansion, through the long corridor filled with many locked rooms and the humming of servers, past staircases and halls, and soon came to the deepest end of the corridor on the second floor: the "rupture point" between the escape pod and the main body of the ship.
At the end of the corridor, everything was still in the same state as when he left last time, the floor, ceiling, and walls as if torn apart by an invisible colossal force, appeared fragmented and broken, outside the rupture point was the endlessly deep dark space, so deep it seemed as if one glance could make a person "fall" in.
Duncan ignored the darkness outside the rupture and came with a clear goal in front of a certain part of the wall on the side of the corridor, soon, he found what he was looking for near that rupture point.
It was a display screen "melted" into the wall, which was still cycling through warnings about the escape pod being released illegally.
"...Now to verify my hypothesis..." Duncan stood in front of the display screen, took a light breath, and slowly closed his eyes, "Let’s ’see’... the true appearance of this place."
A thread of profound starlight seeped out from the slits of his half-closed eyes—he cautiously controlled his increasingly restless "essence", understood his own power, and tried, without fully unleashing the Reverse Singularity, to open his... "other pair of eyes".
Duncan slowly opened Zhou Ming’s eyes.
Starlight burst forth from those eyes, as if ancient stars at this moment suddenly remembered how to revolve, and where the starlight spread, he saw... the other side of Alice’s Mansion.
The astonishingly large ark spaceship floated in the limitless dark chaos of space, the torn starship had almost only a third of its structure left, and he stood at the end of a connecting corridor in the middle of the ship, where the silver-gray and silver-white alloy structure replaced the dark toned floor and walls of the original mansion corridor, various warning lights flickered in the distance, and before his eyes, was the burnt, melted support frame of the escape pod.
A huge hole had been blown open at the front of the escape pod’s release point, looking quite alarming.
"...Lei Nora definitely didn’t leave ’quietly’ as she claimed at that time," Duncan gave the broken pipelines, support frames and the spaceship’s exterior shell that was blasted open only a glance before his lips twitched, "...how did she blow this place open without having any idea what was going on here?"
Of course, nobody in the empty spaceship corridor could answer his questions, after all, the only "owner" and "victim" of this place still didn’t know what an escape pod was—Duncan sighed and just shook his head, then turned his attention back to the flickering display screen.
Now, he had seen the full picture of the device—it was part of the escape pod’s external release system, fixed onto a bent support frame, the entire frame was badly twisted and damaged, its internal piping was even exposed, but it seemed to still be operating normally.
Duncan placed his hand on the device, ready to "read" the data here with his own flame and transfer it to Alice’s side—that was his thought, simple and unrefined.
Alice’s current state was unable to understand the "essence" of her mansion, thus she also couldn’t sense the system malfunction here, the instincts of the "Navigation System Three" were still there but unreactive since Alice couldn’t read the signal, so Duncan’s task was to weld a jumper wire between Alice and the "fault point" of this mansion.
He certainly didn’t understand the principles behind the spaceship—just as most phone repair technicians don’t know the specific internal structure of a chip, as long as bridging wires were soldered on and it worked, that’s all that mattered.
The technique of bridging wires was awe-inspiring.
The flames burned quietly, gradually infiltrating the escape pod’s release system.
Just then, out of the corner of his eye, Duncan suddenly caught sight of something.
A mass... with a dark grey metallic sheen and undulating like mud, seemingly flowing out from the grates and pipes of the surrounding equipment!
That eerie mass of mud-like substance piled up and flowed on the floor, slowly moving towards him, emitting a bone-chilling, low noise. Yet, just as Duncan was raising his guard, ready to react, the mud suddenly stopped not far away, as if observing or judging something.
Duncan paused for a moment, then it dawned on him—
It was the "Cleaner" from Alice’s Mansion! That bizarre shadow used to expel "invading foreign substances"!
...Is this thing a part of the New Hope’s maintenance system? Some kind of damage control device? A swarm of nanomachines?
While maintaining the data intrusion into the escape pod system, Duncan’s mind was racing with thoughts, and just then, he saw the "nanomud" crawl a few steps closer to him.
No hostility whatsoever.
Under Duncan’s cautious gaze, the nanomachine swarm slowly differentiated into an appendage resembling a tentacle, which tapped the release system’s bent support strut as if to demonstrate something to Duncan, pulling a damaged cable out of the strut.
Duncan’s expression was peculiar: "...You mean, connect it here?"
The mud differentiated another limb, swinging it up and down in the air.
Duncan hesitated, then allowed his flames to spread to the damaged cable.
The mud seemed pleased, shaking its two limbs and then reverting to a liquid state. It gurgled as it slowly made its way towards a crack in the nearby wall.
Duncan: "..."
This thing can actually communicate and think?!
While he was still in a daze, the mud had completely left, and right after, he heard Alice’s voice coming through the psychic link: "Captain! The board is lit up! The board is lit up! I think I’ve figured out where that ’escape pod’ is!"
...
"There are one hundred and seventy-six people here—everyone who has ’awakened’ is here," Helena, accompanied by Fenna and Lucresia, walked through the central connecting bridge of the residential area, continuing as they moved, "This was originally part of the power plant at the port. As more and more people ’awoke,’ those who were initially awake and in good condition spontaneously gathered here and built a camp."
Fenna stopped on the connecting bridge, leaning on the railing and looking down at the temporary residential area established using the existing infrastructure of the power plant.
The Female Pope’s voice, after a brief pause, continued: "We’ll soon expand into a better living area—the dormitories next to the power plant. They’re currently occupied by ’confused compatriots’. We can’t expel them by force, and we should avoid conflict as much as possible, but as more and more people in that district awaken, we’ll be able to move our main activity area there once the majority is awake."
"It’s hard to imagine," Lucresia couldn’t help but speak after a moment of silence, "the world has actually turned into this..."
"Better adapt quickly. The current City-State is just this place magnified a thousand times over," Helena said softly. The Female Pope, incarnated and personally stationed at this beacon, turned her head to look at Fenna and Lucresia, "As for now... it’s your turn, tell me about the matters at the end of the world."

chapters.title: Chapter 838 - 835 Cloud
chapters.content:
Chapter 838: Chapter 835 Cloud
The bewildered and blindly ignorant wanderers loiter outside the power plant, the deep rumbling of the port’s power facilities carrying through the dense fog, the icy steam core operating hollowly, with the steam itself becoming a part of the distorted apparition, while the protection of the fire has already vanished into smoke.
But "Shelter" itself has become optional in the world today, the boundary between "normal" and "abnormal" has long been blurred, when all minds fall with the world, "sanity" ironically becomes the madmen and pollution in the eyes of this world—now, the madmen gather within high walls, constructing the last "Shelter," anxiously watching as the outside world gradually succumbs to darkness.
"We will prepare sufficient supplies for the Brilliant Starship," Helena stands on a platform high up in the power plant, saying to Fenna and Lucricia standing beside her, "You can Transition to the western docks—that’s currently one of the external passages we control."
"Can this ’lighthouse’ still provide supplies now?" Lucricia looks at the Female Pope in surprise, "Do you have so many resources?"
"Yes, we’re not short on supplies, this might be a little inconsistent with your first impression of this place," Helena smiles, "But in fact, the entire world’s ’operation’ continues, the production and transportation of various main materials, even the ’commercial activities’ within the City-States... Every half month, a cargo ship full of supplies sails from the border base to refuel this lighthouse and other things, those who have fallen into a daze conduct the handover as usual, while we ’awakeneds’ take out permits from old files to transfer some of the supplies to another warehouse, using the same method, we can also operate many facilities and equipment here."
She turns her head, looking at the vast platform outside the power plant.
"Yes, the world is still running, every part... is operating in a daze along the old trajectory, like a huge ship that has internally collapsed but is still drifting along its original path in the sea under inertia, we who have awakened on this ship have no strength to fix the ship, but at least before it capsizes, we can still ’sail’ with it."
Fenna and Lucricia are silent for a moment, unsure how to respond.
This world has become completely unrecognizable to them.
But Helena obviously doesn’t care, she just waves her hand and continues, "Thanks for informing me about what’s happening at the end of the world, with this, those of us waiting on the big ship now finally know the situation outside, thus waiting now has meaning, no longer just a mere struggle for survival."
"Homeloss... is it still navigating at the ends of the earth?"
"Yes, the captain and Alice are at the ends of the earth, they continue to move toward the farther places," Fenna says softly, "The captain is preparing for the new world, once everything is ready... you can ’blink your eyes’."
"Okay, then I won’t delay your journey any further," Helena’s manifestation turns her head, exhaling lightly, "I’ll go arrange the supplies, and later someone will send you two back to the dock..."
She suddenly stops, staring intently into Fenna’s eyes, only speaking after a long while.
"Fenna, safe travels—see you in our new world."
Fenna nods solemnly, "Yes, Your Holiness, see you in our new world."
...
The howling wind has stopped at some point, leaving only the pure and extreme "cold" lingering on this ice plain—the cold penetrates flesh and seeps into bones, freezing the souls, and among this cold wind, the Fire Transmitters have long forgotten the warmth of "fire."
The undying ones trek across the ice plain, in the cold night, the lanterns on their chests weave a meandering, faintly flickering line deep in the ice field.
Frem stands on hastily built platform, gazing towards the distance of the ice field, at the end of his sight, the towering silhouette of the Church Ark stands silently far away, the lights on the Ark sketching a twinkling "mountain" in the night, while the light from the lanterns flows between this "mountain" and the ice beneath his feet, endlessly coming and going, tireless.
After the ice-breaking device is completely unusable, the Fire Transmitters opened the next section of ice with explosives carried with the ship, and after the explosives ran out, the Ark, with its surging power and sturdy armor, broke open another path, and after that, its power system finally came to a complete halt—even if the steam core is still hollowly howling, the airflow surging in the pipes, the giant vessel still stops between the ice layers, stopping on the last leg before its destination.
But fortunately, it is not far from the final "focus", it is even already within the influence range of the focus—at this moment, civilization’s last "archive" is being established on this ice plain.
Footsteps sound beside him, a veiled priestess walks up to the platform, stops next to Frem, slightly bending over: "Eleven more have ’awakened,’ they’ve been settled in the camp, currently undergoing psychological soothing and guidance."
Frem nods lightly, "Hmm, how are they doing?"
"Better than the last batch," the priestess replies, "Continuously conveying some hints and reminders to those in a ’daze’ state is useful, so when they ’awake,’ most of them almost immediately realize this is still a controlled ’situation,’ and seek help from the nearest contact person... These experiences can be conveyed to the City-State side."
Frem nodded slightly and said nothing more, merely lifting his head to quietly watch the archive building under construction.
Engineering machinery transported from the Ark bustled about on the ice plains, while a cluster of makeshift, even somewhat ugly buildings were beginning to take shape.
Compared to the grandeur of the Ark warship and the ancient solemnity of the onboard Church, these buildings that looked nearly identical to rugged factories possessed virtually no aesthetic appeal, because their sole design goal was to construct the most robust storage space in as short a time as possible in an unfamiliar environment.
A soft murmur came from beside him: "Is this really meaningful?"
Frem turned his head to look at the priestess standing beside him.
"Forgive me, Your Holiness, I am not faltering, I just..." the priestess shook her head, explaining, "I was just thinking about the recent events—more and more people are waking from their ’haze’, and many of them, their last memory even dates back to the day we set off. Many have asked me what happened along the way, so many questions..."
"I understand what you’re trying to say, Delis," Frem quietly interrupted the priestess’s explanations, while his gaze still lingered on that "construction site," "Many people believe that as long as humans survive, everything survives, because civilization itself is created by humans. Humans have created civilization once, they can rebuild it countless times... Yes, I understand, and moreover, I agree—being the Fire Transmitter Pope, I comprehend more than many how civilization is established and sustained."
He paused for a moment, continuing softly: "Civilization without people is meaningless, but, Delis, there’s also the latter part—people without civilization are the same."
"Indeed, civilization is not just the cold stones and books, nor the voiceless sculptures, music scores, and artifacts; those things are merely carriers and manifestations of civilization, not the abstract idea of civilization itself, and there’s no mistake about that, but—
"Civilization needs carriers, it needs evidence.
"To steadfastly cling to ’carriers’ while abandoning ’essence’ is foolish, to only know the essence and think that carriers are unnecessary is also foolish—without carriers and evidence, the most splendid memories will also erode over time, erode before we have the chance to rebuild civilization, and even if not considering it from this angle... Delis, we still need to leave some evidence, so that many years later, future generations can understand what happened in this world.
"One of the meanings of artifacts and archaeology lies in this ’notification’."
The veiled priestess met Frem’s gaze openly, her eyes once bright had turned turbid and dim many days ago, but now, they still remained resolute.
"I understand, I will also convey your admonition to others..."
Frem nodded.
And a thin layer of "fog" had unknowingly formed around them.
Priestess Delis, surprised, raised her head to look at the fluttering white mist surrounding them.
After entering the ice plain, they had not seen "fog" for a long time.
Even though at the edge of their vision lay the magnificent fog wall of the Eternal Veil, unlike other coastal regions, this ice plain was almost never foggy.
"The weather is changing..." She raised her hand, touching the ethereal fog, "Fog on the ice plain now?"
With a furrowed brow, Frem looked up at the sky, observing the drifting, fluid-like wisps of white, and after a moment finally realized.
"No, this isn’t fog," he suddenly spoke, surprise in his voice, "...it’s clouds!"
"Clouds?" The priestess hesitated for a moment, as if pondering what ’clouds’ meant before widening her eyes in astonishment, "Clouds are falling from the sky?"
"...It’s the altitude of the clouds that has lowered," Frem spoke gravely, but he quickly realized that this explanation seemed hardly different, so he added, "All clouds are descending in unison, rather than saying they’re ’falling’, it’s more like..."
He stopped, Delis had already grasped his meaning, blinking uneasily, "The sky itself, is getting lower..."

chapters.title: Chapter 839 - 836: The Clouds Descend
chapters.content:
Chapter 839: Chapter 836: The Clouds Descend
When that day arrives, oceans will forget the appearance of waves, life will forget how to die, flames will not remember how to burn, wind will stop flowing, and clouds will fall from the sky to the sea —— it is the final curtain of the world’s descent, that exiled, from beyond the world, coldly stares at the existence of the Shelter, so percipient of the future of all things.
Around the world, clouds are falling from the sky — or more strictly speaking, a "layer" that includes the "element" of "clouds" is synchronously dropping in altitude.
The falling clouds resemble another flowing sea, gradually closing in overhead, with some lower parts extending to the ground or the sea surface, forming a misty veil, while more of it floats hundreds or even tens of meters above people’s heads. The layering of the sky stops at this height and continues in an extremely slow and nearly imperceptible "descent" process.
Frem stands on the ice plain under the night sky, looking up at the churning clouds so close by, obscured by a thin fog, as if one could touch the magnificent clouds with a raised hand. The Creation of the World’s cold light diffuses through the gaps between the clouds, coating the veil with a mercury-like layer — candidly speaking... it is beautiful.
So breathtaking that it stifles, causing one’s soul to shiver slightly.
Priestess Delis stands next to Frem, along with the Pope, both gazing up at the spectacle in the sky. They have been staring for a long time, as have many others on the ice plain. It’s as if an invisible force has seized everyone by the neck, keeping them in the same posture, rigidly frozen on the ice plain. But suddenly, many start to react, looking around in panic, and many gazes converge on Frem.
"Your Holiness..." Delis finally breaks the silence, her voice hoarse, "What next..."
"We continue our tasks," Frem’s voice rises with calmness as usual, echoing across the plain, "Build the archives, transport the artifacts, preserve our heritage — this world still has a breath left, our work is not yet done."
The Pope’s voice is steady and forceful, like a giant boulder standing on the ice plain, quelling the unrest in everyone’s hearts. The Fire Transmitters fall silent for a moment, then bow their heads, not paying attention to the changes in the sky anymore, but instead continuing to build the archives.
Frem takes a slight breath in a moment unnoticed by all, as his heart beats increasingly faintly, his gaze once again turns to the distance, to the flowing clouds—
Against an extreme backdrop of gray and white, the massive hull of the Homeloss is quietly floating in the "transit passage". Lacking reference elements, the ship seems completely motionless in the center of the passage, but Duncan is well aware that he and his ship are sailing at speeds far beyond human imagination.
The Homeloss has crossed the end of the world. In a sense, Duncan has truly "left the Endless Sea" — left the small sheltered prison constructed by the ancient kings. Beyond this seemingly calm passage lies a place where order is completely gone... a fiery and chaotic graveyard of ashes after the worlds have collapsed.
Duncan feels the connection with the Endless Sea weakening. On the second day that Alice took the helm and steered the Homeloss towards the "Sea of Ashes", he could barely hear the voices of his two "avatars". Now, each day he can only keep those avatars awake for a small amount of time — and they can only perform limited actions during their lucid intervals.
The reasons for this weakening are multifaceted. On one hand, the degree of his "transformation" is deepening; on the other hand, the actual "distance" between the Homeloss and those avatars is extending. The remaining reasons... may relate to that Sea of Ashes mentioned by Lei Nora, and the special environment in the Sea of Ashes.
The only good news is that the "Strengthening Mark" he deliberately left on Nina and others, specifically to maintain contact in this situation, is still effective. Because the functionality of the mark is extremely specialized and simple, it has not been much affected by the aforementioned changes, allowing him to still contact his crew members.
After completing today’s routine check, Duncan is strolling on the Homeloss. He walks past empty corridors, through quiet stairways, and arrives on the deserted deck — Alice is currently at the helm at the stern, with the absence of the puppets’ company, the ship in front of him seems completely returned to the state it was when he first arrived.
Everywhere is empty, everywhere is quiet, the first time he pushed open the door of the Displaced, he saw such a scene.
Of course, some things have changed — back then, his mind wasn’t as noisy as it is now.
"Hey, Cap’n, let me tell you, we took away a lot of good stuff from that lighthouse! That woman named Helena was so freaking generous, she let me raid the warehouse, and I found some beautiful dresses... not sure why someone like her would collect pretty dresses... too bad I can’t wear them, they’re two sizes too big..."
This uneducated and crude voice is Sherry’s.
"Uncle Duncan, everything is fine here, Niru and I have become good friends, I even sewed her a small dress... Please take care of yourself on the ship, and make sure Alice eats on time when she’s at the helm, I left a lot of biscuits and jam in the kitchen..."
This considerate and gentle voice is Nina’s.
"Captain, I haven’t been slacking these past few days, Miss Lukrecia can vouch for me, I’ve started to help her crew clean the decks and corridors — I was never this diligent on the White Oak..."
This hoarse voice belongs to a sailor.
"Dad, don’t let him fool you. He’s been forced to work by Luny—it’s him who lazes around in the warehouse all day long, even trying to seduce my servants into joining his big nap. Luny couldn’t stand it anymore... This guy even demanded a daily wage from me on the grounds that laboring on the Brilliant Starship wasn’t covered in the contract!"
This resentful voice belongs to Lucracia.
Duncan stopped on the middle deck, listening helplessly to the noisy commotion in his mind, and finally couldn’t help but speak out, "Sounds like it’s quite lively over there."
"Having one Sherry is enough to make it as lively as a battlefield," Lucracia’s voice full of resentments echoed in Duncan’s mind, "She even incites others to mess around with her. Yesterday, she even tricked Niru into crawling into the bedside cabinet. I had to dismantle the entire cabinet to rescue the little one! How do you usually put up with it?"
"Usually, I think it’s okay," Duncan thought for a moment and said seriously, "It’s quite nice to have some liveliness on the ship—although it might be a bit too stimulating for you."
Lucracia sighed longly: "Well, the most exhilarating has to be Miss Fenna’s morning exercise noises... But I can’t really say whether that’s more thrilling compared to Nina’s frights and explosions."
Listening to his daughter’s resentful rambling, Duncan’s expression twitched subtly, remembering that he had to admit that the chaos on the Homeloss was indeed a bit severe...
Then after a while, he heard Maurice’s voice.
"Captain, how’s the situation over there?"
"Homeloss is still in the ’passage’," Duncan looked up at the situation outside the bulwarks and casually said, "Frankly, it’s difficult now to analyze from a ’distance’ or ’course’ perspective where exactly this ship is positioned, even Alice can’t be sure—but one thing is certain, we are moving towards the coordinates signal sent by Lei Nora, that Alice can still sense."
"...I never expected that, usually, the most unreliable one on the ship is now doing the most important thing," Sherry couldn’t help but mutter, "In the end, it’s her accompanying you to the end of the world..."
As Sherry’s voice fell, there was sudden silence from the others. After two or three seconds, Duncan heard Sherry’s loud complaining, "Hey, what kind of reaction is this! Am I not more reliable than Alice! I’m usually so obedient and well-behaved... Nina, don’t you turn your head!"
Duncan outright ignored the commotion from Sherry’s side.
"How’s the situation on the Endless Sea?"
It was quiet for two or three seconds on the other end, and then Maurice’s voice came through: "As we reported earlier today, the clouds have fallen from the sky—now the entire Endless Sea is covered with a thin layer of ’fog’, with heavy clouds looming above... Frankly, if I didn’t know what this scene signifies, it would indeed be a magnificent sight."
"The good news is that besides the lowering of the clouds, no worse changes have happened, at least the navigation of the ships is not affected," Fenna’s voice followed immediately, "We are now heading towards the direction of Ploand, Miss Lucracia plans to take us there first, then she will return to Light Breeze Harbor with Brilliant Starship and stay there till the end.
"Moreover, we have also contacted Mr. Tirian. After reaching the mid-sea area, a ’Sun Fleet’ will depart from Ploand and head north, Miss Agatha will transfer to that ship to head to Frost.
"As for the ’sailor’, Captain Lawrence in Feyron has also made arrangements. He will be contacting the City-State Confederation’s management personnel later—if the confederation is still functioning by then—and then the sailor will be sent to Feyron to rendezvous with the White Oak Ship.
"And if by then the operation of the City-State Confederation has foundered, the White Oak Ship will personally go to Ploand to pick up the sailor."
Having said this, Fenna paused for a few seconds, then slowly continued—
"Captain, please rest assured, we will do well and will not disappoint you."

chapters.title: Chapter 840 - 837: Be Quiet, Thinking
chapters.content:
Chapter 840: Chapter 837: Be Quiet, Thinking
Duncan listened silently to the voices in his heart, the calm and reliable reports from Fenna and Morris, the helpless complaints from Lucy Lecia, and sometimes the noisy chattering of Sherry and the nagging of Nina—these voices that crossed the vast stretches of space and time seemed like temperature-laden anchors that, even after his two "avatars" left in the City-State were gradually becoming ineffective, still firmly anchored him on the side of reason and humanity.
After that, he temporarily ended the communication with Fenna and others, slowly walked across the entire deck, passed through the staircase and ramp at the stern, and arrived at the towering helm at the stern.
The puppet still stood quietly at the helm, her hands tightly gripping the black and heavy steering wheel, her focus-less eyes staring straight ahead, while countless invisible threads stretched out from her body, connecting her to the Homeloss beneath her feet and to the ethereal projection of the New Hope up high in the sky.
Thin mists suddenly began to spread from all directions on the deck, flowing and converging.
Duncan noticed the eerily appearing mist and subconsciously furrowed his brows, and right after, he realized that the gray-white backdrop in the distance seemed to have gradually "cracked" open—patches and patches of fog emerged at the end of the uniform "corridor", and deep within the mist was a sense of emptiness.
Almost at that instant, he heard that intermittent, vague voice: "Jump complete..."
The Homeloss experienced a slight shake, not as obvious of a vibration as when it had previously reached the border node and entered some kind of "medium," the passageway silently shattered, and the endless, thin mist filled the surroundings in the blink of an eye; the next second, Alice, who was at the helm, blinked her eyes, and the puppet’s consciousness suddenly returned to her body.
"Captain!" Miss Puppet looked at Duncan, her face instantly bloomed with a happy and credit-seeking smile, "We’ve arrived!"
Duncan nodded, but just as he was about to speak, he suddenly froze—he noticed that the edges of the Homeloss were becoming rapidly "blurred"!
No, not just the edges, the entire ship was quickly going "blurry"! Enveloped by the mist, everything in his field of vision seemed to have suddenly lost clear "boundaries", the details on the deck began to disappear, the masts grew dim in the fog, and even Alice right in front of him, seemed to be fusing with the mist and was rapidly transforming into some kind of ethereal form.
And that pale green flame enveloping the whole body of the Homeloss also dissipated in the process!
Alice, sensing something, stood there in shock, then slowly lowered her head, looking at her hands that were rapidly losing detail and becoming "blurry": "...Eh?"
But the next second, Zhou Ming-Duncan suddenly reacted.
Starry light began to suffuse the pale green flame that enveloped the whole body of the Homeloss, Duncan’s eyes seemed to shine with a billion stars, and the Homeloss, which had been on the verge of information collapse, rapidly reassembled and regained definition in his vision—under the flame burning with pervasive starlight, the deck and masts almost instantaneously returned to their original state, and Alice’s figure also stabilized in front of his eyes.
The puppet hardly had time to react to what had happened when she saw the ship’s flame suddenly "change color", and then the same flames surrounded her. After being stunned for a few seconds, she finally raised her hand to look at it and exclaimed in amazement: "Wow—"
Yet Duncan still felt a bit of an after-shock in his heart, he took a light breath, and for the first time truly sensed something substantial about the "Ashen Edge" that Lei Nora had discovered.
This is the true boundary of order, the frontier of nothingness, the "Primordial Sea" where information units are not yet assigned a value. Here, information has yet to be defined, and any "creation" from within the Shelter, even the Homeloss returning from subspace, can’t stable exist here as a "data structure"—because there are no data structures here at all!
Perhaps only beings that have survived the great annihilation and achieved "self-stabilization" on the informational level can maintain relative "safety and stability" in this place.
Such as the "Reverse Singularity," such as the wreckage of the New Hope.
Duncan took a deep breath, calming his emotions, and gently patted Alice’s hair; he then looked around—speaking of the wreckage of the New Hope, where is Lei Nora?
He and his ship had already arrived at the position of the escape pod’s signal, but as he looked around from the towering stern deck, he saw no solid entities in this chaotic and void "fog."
"Can you sense the signal from the escape pod?" Duncan asked Alice with a frown, "We should be in the right place, right?"
"Yeah, theoretically it should be right here," the doll finally snapped out of her fascination with the surrounding beautiful starlight, quickly sensed the position of the escape pod, then scratched her head in confusion, "The signal is nearby... I just sensed it, why can’t I see it..."
Duncan’s lips suddenly twitched: "Don’t tell me we’ve knocked her flying again..."
Upon hearing this, Alice was startled and keenly caught the key word: "Again?"
Duncan: "...You don’t need to worry about that. Let’s find Lei Nora first."
As he spoke, he slowly released his perception, cautiously controlling his own power that belonged to the "Reverse Singularity," trying to detect any unusual aura around the Homeloss.
At this moment, he had two thoughts in mind—the first was that he hoped the unfortunate Frost Queen hadn’t really been knocked away by the Homeloss, and the second was that he hoped the unfortunate Frost Queen hadn’t been crushed under the hull of the massive ship...
He had come to meet with the queen, not to let the queen "run into a stroke of luck." It wouldn’t just be awkward if they met later, explaining would also be difficult.
By this time, Alice had also realized, and after racking her brain for a while, Ms. Doll slapped her hand: "Oh right... the Homeloss came directly according to the escape pod’s signal, so if it landed, wouldn’t it have landed right on top of the escape pod..."
Duncan sighed deeply—what’s the use of realizing it now.
Had he known, he wouldn’t have let Alice teleport directly to the escape pod’s beacon; he should have set a "distance from teleportation marker XX" for a safe distance. But how could he have expected that the New Hope’s beacon was such an accurate thing? When the Homeloss went to the Four Gods node before, it didn’t crash directly onto Their foreheads...
And just when he felt such a sigh in his heart, Duncan really sensed something.
He "scanned" an "entity" that did not belong to the Homeloss.
But the location of that entity... was right on board the Homeloss.
Duncan raised his head in confusion, looked towards the direction he perceived, and after a moment of confirmation, a subtle expression gradually took over his face.
Alice also noticed: "Ah, Captain, have you found something?"
"Let’s go check it out first." Muttering this, Duncan left the cockpit with Alice, crossing platforms and stairways, following the guidance of his senses, they finally arrived in front of the door to the captain’s quarters at the stern of the ship.
Alice lifted her head to look at the familiar place in front of her, holding her head with both hands: "This is the captain’s quarters, I don’t see anything else."
Duncan, however, still stared intently at the door of the captain’s quarters (The Displaced’s Door), he sensed the changes that had happened here, and even... gradually understood the changes that occurred.
After frowning and pondering for quite some time, he finally took a step forward and placed his hand by the... hinge side of The Displaced’s Door.
The twisted and dislocated time-space structure emerged in his mind, morphing into a real mapping that could be deciphered; he found the node of this spatial dislocation and gently pushed with his hand.
The door opened - pushed open from the position of the hinges.
Alice watched this scene with her mouth agape, and after a long while managed to exclaim, "You can open it from there?!"
Duncan: "...Be quiet, I’m thinking."
Behind the door glowed a misty halo, seemingly a "room" that didn’t belong to the Homeloss, shrouded by a layer of continuously trembling optical phenomenon.
Unlike the "normal" process of being directly teleported to the "bachelor apartment" after pushing open The Displaced’s Door, what appeared before Duncan this time seemed to be a concrete "entrance", an entrance that could even allow entities other than him to enter.
He first reached into the halo with his hand to test it out, then turned his head to look at Alice: "Do you want to come?"
Alice nodded without hesitation: "Yes!"
Duncan reached out to the doll-like lady: "Follow me - hold onto my arm, and don’t let go until it’s confirmed safe."
