Alice obediently grabbed Duncan’s arm and followed the captain towards the hazy glow.
It was as if they had passed through a layer of icy curtain, after a very brief moment of dizziness and sensory disorientation, the sight in front of them stabilized rapidly.
A grand and spacious room appeared before Duncan and Alice, real and solid underfoot.
Lei Nora sat on the large bed in the middle of the room with a somewhat vacant expression, staring blankly at Duncan and Alice who "entered" through the door — the Frost Queen seemed to have just received a huge impact, appearing to be in a stupefied state, until Duncan approached her, then she suddenly reacted and raised her hands, gesturing in the air.
"...They just rolled right in!"
Lei Nora’s expression gradually grew a little frantic.
"Such a huge ship! It just came barreling towards me head-on! Half the room was smashed to pieces by a mess of things, and it took a good long while to recover, then you pushed through the wall and walked in! Such a big hole! Couldn’t you use the door?"
Pushed through the wall?
Duncan was momentarily stunned and looked back at the direction they had come from.
He saw Lei Nora’s room door, the door that was nicely set in the wall, which was still shut tight, but next to the door on the wall, there was a big hole — that was where he and Alice had entered.
Spatial dislocation.jpg.
Alice quietly poked Duncan’s arm: "Captain, why aren’t you saying anything?"
"...Be quiet, I’m thinking again."

chapters.title: Chapter 841 - 838: Invitation at Century’s End
chapters.content:
Chapter 841: Chapter 838: Invitation at Century’s End
On the fringes of order, the composition and operational laws of information present a state that is bizarre and varied—Duncan thought hard for half a day and decided to give up thinking.
The good news right now is that Lei Nora wasn’t flung out by the Homeloss, nor was she crushed under the ship’s hull—the bad news is that she was struck "into" the ship, and at this time, she was still in a daze.
This reminded Duncan of a famous painting of the world:
Dog that got hit by a car and ended up embedded into the bumper and taken onto the highway.jpg.
Duncan coughed twice and tossed the slightly out-of-tune association in his mind to the side. He and Alice took two steps forward, with an apologetic and concerned expression on his face: "Sorry, I wasn’t careful when steering the ship... Are you alright?"
Alice, who was beside him, bowed her head, seemingly pondering something, then suddenly poked Duncan’s arm: "Captain, I remember that it was the Homeloss that collided with the White Oak, and then I came aboard your ship. Now it’s the Frost Queen’s turn. Does that not make it come full circle?"
Duncan immediately glared: "’Coming full circle’ isn’t used like this!"
Lei Nora seemed to recover a bit at this time. She rubbed her swollen head, getting used to it as she stood up from the bedside: "It’s fine, the impact was just a bit strong—I didn’t expect your way of appearing to be so... ’shocking’."
As she spoke, her gaze already fell on Alice next to her. With a slightly unusual and complex look, she closely examined this doll that almost exactly resembled her. The latter also turned her gaze over, looking seriously and curiously at Lei Nora.
After a long time, Lei Nora suddenly revealed a smile and extended her hand to Alice: "Hello."
Alice also smiled happily, seizing Lei Nora’s hand and shaking it vigorously: "Hello there!"
"It’s unbelievable," Lei Nora quietly admired the doll’s grip strength, then turned to Duncan, "I never expected that my first encounter with Alice in the realm of reality would be under such circumstances... although it’s hard to say if this place truly counts as ’reality’."
While she spoke, she subtly withdrew her hand and turned to face another wall in the room, waving her hand at it.
The wall silently "shattered" in the blink of an eye, transforming into a transparent curtain. Beyond this curtain was endless nothingness, as well as the chaotic mist floating and filling the emptiness.
"I’ve been waiting here for a very long time," Lei Nora slowly began as she looked at the "scenery" outside, "During this time I attempted to ’sail’ along the edge of this dense fog, but found nothing. There’s only this sort of chaotic and empty fog—actually at the start, I couldn’t even see the mist, only sense that there was some ’thing’ existing here. It was only after making contact with you last time that I gained the ability to observe this fog, but that’s all there is to it."
"Don’t tell me you’ve tried to venture deeper into the ’fog’," Duncan looked at Lei Nora with an odd expression, "That would be quite reckless."
"Don’t worry, although I’m now enthusiastic about exploring, I haven’t lost my mind," Lei Nora said with a smile, shaking her head, "The dangers of the deeper parts are unimaginable. Even with the protection of the ’drifting abode’, it’s likely I wouldn’t be able to come back alive if I went in."
"Your judgment is rational," Duncan breathed out a little, "That place is a completely undefined and unassigned ’primitive data ocean’; any entity that enters would be instantaneously wiped clean to the same unassigned state—it’s not the same concept as this ’border’ state we’re in now."
Lei Nora nodded slightly, then looked at Duncan with some curiosity: "Now that you’re here, what are you planning to do next?"
"First, confirm my speculations, then conduct some research and tests to see if it’s possible to create some ’samples’ in this primitive data ocean," Duncan said immediately, clearly having plans in mind. Then he looked curiously at the Frost Queen before him, "But what I’m more curious about right now is... whether you can leave this room."
Lei Nora was taken aback for a moment: "Leave this place?"
While speaking, she looked up towards the doorway-shaped hole that had been left when Duncan and Alice pushed through the wall to enter the room—the softly glowing "passageway" was still steadily in existence.
"You mean..." She gradually realized, "to accompany you to the Homeloss?"
"It’s a portal that allows stable passage, although it seems a bit strange the way it’s been opened," Duncan nodded, "I feel that it can accommodate people to come and go freely, but I’m not sure whether you are an ’entity’ that can leave this room."
"...I believe I can," Lei Nora frowned slightly, thought over it seriously, and said, "I’ve reached out my hand through that door before to catch the ’intangible things’ from this sea of ashes, and I’ve left the room before to enter your ’palace’ floating in the endless void—I might be bound as part of this ’drifting house,’ but as long as I do not stray too far, there doesn’t seem to be a problem."
"That’s good to hear," Duncan said, a smile appearing on his face as he extended his hand in an inviting gesture, "Would you like to come aboard the Homeloss as a guest?"
The Frost Queen too revealed a smile, slightly inclining in a bow: "The honor is all mine."
Once again passing through that slightly cool curtain, after feeling the familiar slight dizziness and sensory displacement, Duncan and Alice returned to the deck of the Homeloss.
Then Duncan turned back to confirm, and saw that Lei Nora had indeed successfully passed through that doorway—she stood in front of the "Portal of the Displaced," her expression seemingly still a bit bewildered.
Lei Nora’s eyes widened; even though she had been prepared, the moment she truly passed through that door, she couldn’t avoid feeling momentarily disoriented.
Now, she was standing solidly on the deck of Homeloss, an expansive "world" surrounding her. Everything within her view seemed so real, and... "spacious."
She had stepped out of her cage.
"I..." Lei Nora’s lips moved a few times, and after a while, she finally spoke, "I actually walked out of the room..."
"Welcome to my ship. Before we set off to explore this vast Ashen Sea, let me give you a tour here," Duncan said with a smile, spreading his arms in a welcoming gesture, "It’s quite empty now, might seem a bit desolate, but it used to be very lively."
Lei Nora listened in a daze, and finally adjusting her mentality, she stretched vigorously outside her cage with a faint smile.
"It feels so good to be out."
She said softly, then turned to glance back in the direction she had come from.
The door of The Displaced, which had been pushed open from the hinge, stood silently in her view.
Duncan noticed that Lei Nora had suddenly become still and casually asked, "What are you thinking about?"
"...I am pondering..."
"Ahem, this door is quite magical. Through different methods of opening, it can re-establish a ’passage’ amidst the chaotic relations of time and space," Duncan coughed twice, putting on a serious professional face as he explained, "But you only need to know two ways to open it — pulling it normally from the door handle leads to my captain’s cabin, and pushing it from the hinge position, as it is now, connects to your Drifting House."
Lei Nora blinked, unable to contain her curiosity, she asked: "What’s the principle behind it?"
After some thought, Duncan continued with a straight face: "Because it’s magical."
Lei Nora immediately stopped asking questions.
Duncan then stepped forward to close "The Displaced’s Door" in the normal way. After restoring it to its normal state, he pulled on the handle to open the door to the captain’s cabin.
He turned around and gestured for Lei Nora to enter.
In the captain’s cabin, the black wooden carved goat’s head on the navigation table, hearing the noise, immediately turned its neck with a squeak, and saw the figures coming through the door, first catching sight of the Frost Queen walking side by side with Alice.
It visibly paused, and then exclaimed in surprise, "Whoa! I’m sure that’s not two Miss Alices — Captain, you’ve brought an impressive guest."
"This is my first mate," Duncan introduced with a hand gesture, "Its name is Saslouka, but you can just call it Goat Head."
Then he pointed to Lei Nora and said to Goat Head, "This is the Frost Queen. No need for much introduction — never mind the theory and the process, in the end, she’s on the ship now, a guest here for the time being."
"Hello, Mr. First Mate, you can just call me Lei Nora," said Lei Nora politely with a nod, but then she paused, as if a realization faintly dawned on her, "Wait a minute... Saslouka? That name sounds familiar to me..."
"That’s all from youth," Goat Head suddenly shook its head with dignity, speaking with a tone full of vicissitudes, "Back then I was whole, with a body beneath my head... but now I’m just the first mate of this ship, Captain Duncan’s most loyal first mate."
While speaking, it stretched its neck vigorously toward the other side, pointing with its chin to another "goat head" (Skull of Dreams) on the opposite side of the navigation table: "This is also Saslouka, my other head, but this one has a malfunction and can’t communicate right now. Usually, it’s just me talking to it — it’s a fine listener, silent and patient; the captain always tells me I talk too much and to shut up, but this head never does. And let me tell you, I’ve always felt that this head indeed responds. Sometimes when I talk to it a lot, it even moves a little, but the captain always says that’s my imagination..."
"Shut up."
"Yes, Captain."
Lei Nora looked on with a somewhat blank expression, not having processed what had just happened. She felt like a wall of words without punctuation marks had just come rolling towards her...
The last time she had felt such an impact was a few dozen minutes before; at that time, it had been the Homeloss coming her way...

chapters.title: Chapter 842 - 839 "Test
chapters.content:
Chapter 842: Chapter 839 "Test
This is an incredible ship—with an incredible captain, an incredible first mate, and an incredible pigeon.
There’s also an equally incredible, and identical-looking doll on the ship.
Lei Nora found this place completely different from what she had imagined—yet somewhat better.
After a round on the upper deck, Duncan led the "Frost Queen" back to the main deck.
"This ship is huge; there are layers and layers of cabins below the deck. A full tour might take more than a day," he said with a smile, "but for now, let’s focus on the more pressing matters."
Hearing the captain’s words, Lei Nora’s thoughts quickly shifted back from her admiration for the ship, and she promptly adjusted her expression, looking seriously outside the bulwark of Homeloss.
The apparently ordinary, thin and gentle mist flowed outside the ship’s bulwark, quiet and harmless.
But it wasn’t mist at all—there was no "mist" beyond Homeloss. In the space outside, there was only supreme nothingness, beyond cognition and description. The supposed "mist" was merely a weak illusion triggered by the very limited human perception vaguely sensing the presence of "something."
But the "captain" said that hidden within this supreme void were the keystones of new worlds.
Lei Nora’s gaze couldn’t help but fall on Duncan, knowing that another true existence was concealed within that tall and majestic figure. The "Multifaceted Starlight" was looking into the distance through this body, his expression serious, as if sensing and searching for something in the flowing mist.
Duncan Zhouming stepped towards the edge of the deck, his perception diffused across the whole ship, and using the ship as a medium, he cautiously "touched" the invisible "Sea of Ash" outside, watching the remnants of a world that had been extinguished among the flowing mist.
A moment later, he reached out over the bulwark—his fingertips covered with strands of flame, within which quietly steeped the colors of starlight.
He heard a fuzzy noise and a tremor coming from the depths of Homeloss; the masts and ropes creaked, and within these sounds seemed to mix a certain restlessness.
"Don’t worry," Duncan murmured to himself, "I am still your captain."
The anxious creaks and tremors subsided slightly.
Duncan’s fingers then touched the "area" outside the bulwark for the first time.
Almost simultaneously, a fluttering sound of beating wings came from above, as Ai Yi descended from the mast with a grand entrance and landed on Duncan’s shoulder. It flapped its wings vigorously, emitting a series of sharp and strange female voices: "Kerchunk... hot hot hot hot hot hot hot hot..."
Then the pigeon hopped off Duncan’s shoulder, seemingly frantic or excited, and scurried across the deck flapping its wings and squawking incomprehensible things that no one except Duncan Zhouming could understand—leaving Lei Nora staring in astonishment.
"...What is this pigeon saying?" Lei Nora couldn’t help but touch the doll beside her, though conversing with a doll with her own exact appearance felt eerily weird. In this place, she found no one else to ask, "Hot... what?"
"Oh, Ai Yi has its own way of speaking," Alice gestured as if it was the most natural thing, "It’s conveying some very important matters to the captain."
Lei Nora was taken aback and looked at the doll in astonishment: "...You can understand it?"
Alice, even more confident than before: "Of course not."
Falling silent at the response, Lei Nora was speechless: "..."
Noticing the sudden silence beside her, Alice turned curiously towards the "Frost Queen," "Hey? Why have you stopped talking?"
"...I wish I had your attitude back in the day," Lei Nora sighed, her thoughts drifting to the past, "I used to live... so tiredly."
"Then just try to live more relaxed from now on," Alice immediately smiled and patted Lei Nora’s arm, "After all, those tiring days are over."
Lei Nora suddenly felt that perhaps this seemingly naive doll possessed a different kind of wisdom in life...
Duncan heard the conversation behind him, but he paid it no mind—most of his attention was now on the "world" outside the bulwark, on those deep ashes.
Slowly retracting his hand, Zhou Ming opened his eyes towards the mist, ancient starlight extended in his field of vision, and where his gaze landed... he saw the unassigned primal information elements undergoing changes under the immersion of the starlight.
After a period of contemplation, he spread his hands towards a particular direction.
Lei Nora and Alice’s conversation came to an abrupt stop—when the sounds of wind and flowing mountain springs came from that direction, they instantly widened their eyes in astonishment.
In that hazy fog, something appeared. A massive, colorless and detail-less grey mountain range materialized out of the clouds. The mountain then rapidly transformed, like a living thing, its surface beginning to feature valleys, gradually coloring, and various sounds came from that direction, now distant, now close, sometimes real, sometimes illusory.
Duncan Zhouming stood at the edge of the deck, information reassembling before his eyes, being redefined in his thoughts. He raised his hand and made a small adjustment as if tuning strings, and the "mountain" that was quickly gaining substance suddenly split in the middle—a magnificent waterfall poured down the chasm, flowing into a river—in the next second, the river surged, vast plains emerged on either side of the great river, a land more extensive than any City-State Lei Nora ever knew of grew and spread through the fog, the mists cleared, and clouds and blue sky gathered...
Everything newly born was rapidly expanding and finally spread to the surroundings of the Homeloss, where a great river flowed into a vast lake, and the Homeloss floated on the mirror-like surface of the lake. A few seconds later, "wind" was created and brought into this scene, causing ripples to appear on the surface of the lake.
Lei Nora watched this scene in astonishment, and finally could not help herself from coming to the edge of the deck, gazing at the greenery and blue sky that had spread to the horizon, as if the whole world had been fashioned complete, along with the lakes and mountains. She smelled the fresh air, heard the sounds of wind and water, and a strong feeling surged in her heart—
That this place truly existed, everything here was real and "valid," and at this very moment, if a person were to come to this vibrant lakeshore, then... he could survive here!
He could breathe here, drink the water, crops could grow in the soil, birds and beasts could reproduce in the mountains and plains, rain would fall, clouds would gather and disperse in the wind, plants would flourish and wither, the cycle of life would revolve...
A joyous smile was about to bloom on her face.
But before that smile could emerge, Duncan Zhouming had already lowered his hands.
And so, everything around the Homeloss silently collapsed and dissipated into nothingness—the mountains and plains instantly reverted back to mist, all color and shape returned to chaos, and the sounds and the breezes that brushed the cheeks... it was as if they had never existed.
Lei Nora looked dazedly at this scene, seemingly unable to react for a moment. After a while, she finally looked up towards the captain’s direction.
"This was just a test, and the most elementary test at that," Duncan walked towards Lei Nora, his voice deep, "only to verify whether the ’materials’ here could be revitalized again—Creation is not like this."
Lei Nora detected a complexity in the captain’s tone, and felt nervous inside: "Then... the result of the test..."
"Good news and bad news," Duncan exhaled softly and began slowly, "The good news is, my earlier judgment was correct, information does not disappear, it merely loses its original ’definition.’ Reassigning it can get this mathematical machine running again."
Lei Nora’s tone was urgent: "And the bad news?"
"The bad news is that another judgment of mine was also correct—the existing conditions cannot sustain this rebooted mathematical machine to ’self-sustain.’ Just like you saw just now, once it loses my observation and definition, everything here will instantly revert to its initial state.
"So to simply reassign them is meaningless, everything must go back to the ’singularity.’ I need a beginning big bang, and a big bang... requires stringent conditions."
Lei Nora tried to follow the captain’s train of thought, the knowledge she had acquired in that "Nest" began turning over in her mind again, and after pondering for a moment, she started to grasp it: "You... know what conditions it needs?"
Duncan was silent for a bit and then nodded: "... Yes."
"Can you do it? Is it very difficult, or is it simply impossible?"
This time, Duncan did not answer her question. After a long period of contemplation, he just shook his head gently: "I need to think about it more."
Afterwards, he waved his hand to Lei Nora and Alice.
"I’m going back to my room to plan out the next steps," he sighed and turned towards the stern of the ship, "There are many empty rooms below deck, Alice can take you to rest."
As Duncan walked away, Lei Nora blinked and turned to the doll beside her: "He seems very preoccupied, is the ’captain’ always so... human-like?"
She had thought for a long time to find a suitable word like "human-like," and had not dared to say it in front of Duncan.
"Yeah," Alice nodded without much thought, "Sherry said the captain is very human-like!"
Lei Nora: "...?"
Is "human-like" supposed to be used that way?!
But before the Frost Queen could speak up, Alice had already swiftly changed the subject: "I’ll take you to the room on the ship to rest first... Oh, do you want to drink fish soup?"
Lei Nora was bewildered by the abrupt shift in topic and answered after a pause, "Er, no need."
Alice was still full of enthusiasm: "The fish soup is delicious! It’s a signature dish on this ship!"
"Thank you, but I... probably won’t have the fortune to enjoy it."
"You don’t like fish? What about sweet pancakes? The captain likes sweet pancakes the best!"
Lei Nora looked embarrassed: "...but I’m a ghost right now."
"... Oh."

chapters.title: Chapter 843 - 840 Lei Nora is Greatly Shocked
chapters.content:
Chapter 843: Chapter 840 Lei Nora is Greatly Shocked
The goat-headed figure emitted a slight creak from below its head, its neck turning slowly atop its pedestal, silently observing Duncan as he returned to the captain’s quarters, its gaze following the captain’s movements.
Upon reaching the chart table, Duncan sat in the high-backed chair, hands bracing the table’s surface. The maritime chart on the table was shrouded in a swirling mist, rendering everything hazy. It seemed even this incredible chart had lost its reference value in this "sea area," which had long crossed the boundaries of the known world.
Yet Duncan’s attention was clearly not on the chart clouded by mist—his eyes were focused on a far more distant place, as if peering through the table and floor of this room, contemplating the vast emptiness beyond the Homeloss.
After a while, the goat-headed figure finally ventured cautiously, "I noticed just now... The ’environment’ around the Homeloss has undergone significant changes. Was that your doing?"
Perhaps influenced by the atmosphere, the typically boisterous first mate this time refrained from unnecessary chatter.
"I conducted some tests," Duncan murmured, "I verified the hypothesis that information is imperishable, and confirmed that information within this ’Sea of Ashes’ can still sustain the operation of things... In the brief test, ripples of change did indeed reappear in this cooled ash."
"But they didn’t last, did they?" The goat head hesitated, "I felt it... the emergence and fading away of this ’ripple’ you mentioned. Although I don’t understand the principles and processes involved, I can sense that there’s something missing behind those changes."
"The Prime Mover, a process that can instantaneously reset and fully reboot the entire ’mathematical machine’," Duncan did not conceal the knowledge he had touched upon in that brief "ripple," "To put it simply, short-term, localized grants to a portion of the raw materials in this Sea of Ashes are futile. The overall ’entropification’ of the Sea of Ashes is causing all changes to revert to zero, so if we truly want to transform the ’raw materials’ here into a new world, we need to reset the entire system—which might be relatively easier than figuring out how to ’import’ saved data from the old world during the reset process."
The goat head was silent for a long time. After much contemplation, it slowly lifted its head, "I’m not sure what you mean by ’entropification,’ but it sounds like you are considering some rather dire solutions. Forgive my frankness, Captain... Miss Nina would be heartbroken. You made a promise to her."
Duncan remained silent, merely watching the goat head atop the table.
"You believe you are the most suitable ’Prime Mover’, is that it?" The goat head seemed to have missed the captain’s gaze, continuing on, "Resetting the entire ’mathematical machine’ sounds like an enormous amount of energy and ’information’ would be required, and you possess both these qualities ’within yourself’..."
"That’s why I’m considering alternative solutions," Duncan calmly interrupted the goat head.
The neck of the goat head made a series of creaks and groans, clearly taken aback, "...I thought you were planning for self-sacrifice..."
"Yes, I have considered that, but Bartok reminded me of something before he left," Duncan spoke with a serene expression, "One should not easily use sacrifice to lay the foundation for a new world—sacrifice should always be the very last resort, not the primary plan. To sacrifice too readily degrades its very own essence—and besides, I promised Nina and Lucy that I would return home."
As he spoke, he took a deep breath.
"Of course, if there truly were no other choice, I would not shirk from death, but for now... I believe I should strive harder to find a better solution."
"Do you have an idea?" The goat head asked with sudden curiosity, "Do you have an alternate method to ’initiate’ the process?"
"In theory, what I need is only information and energy, and since the ’information’ part can actually be completed by a later grant, what I really need is energy—the energy to restart the mathematical machine and get ’information’ running," Duncan said slowly as he thought, "I already have a vague idea on how to solve this, but whether it’s feasible..."
He suddenly paused, seemingly gazing at some non-existent entity in a certain direction, pondering for a moment before continuing, "I think I need to talk to a certain someone I made plans with."
While speaking, he casually asked, "What’s Alice doing right now?"
The goat head was momentarily stunned, briefly checked on the ship’s situation, and a subtly human expression appeared on its stiff wooden face, "...She’s currently leading the Frost Queen around, preparing to do something really weird..."
If even the goat head found the situation to be weird—it must indeed be very strange.
On the spacious mid-deck, Alice was leading Lei Nora to appreciate her newest triumph learned only recently—the doll was so pleased with herself, dragging the befuddled Frost Queen onto a barrel, then pointing to her own head, "I’ve just learned this! It took me so long to get it right with Luny!"
But before Lei Nora could react, the puppet embraced her own head and yanked upwards; with a ’pop’, her head was tossed into the air.
Then she moved her body below, adjusting her position left and right, using her neck joint to aim at her falling head in mid-air...
It wasn’t until then that Lei Nora finally understood what the puppet intended to do—but she felt like she might as well have remained ignorant.
And what’s worse, the puppet hadn’t caught it yet.
Her head tumbled down, crown first—thumping solidly onto her neck joint with a "thud," then rolling on the ground all the way to Lei Nora’s feet, looking up innocently and blinking, "Just... just a minor, tiny... mistake, help me pick... pick it up..."
Lei Nora’s eye twitched as she watched this unfold, despite being the Frost Queen who had once presided over the Abyss Project and faced rebels without batting an eyelid, she now seemed to be struggling to keep her composure.
Duncan arrived on deck just in time to witness the scene.
He felt a great shock—though probably less so than what Lei Nora felt.
Then he quickly stepped forward, grabbed Alice’s head and pressed it back onto her neck joint, and only after a "pop" sound did he turn to look at the still confused Lei Nora, wearing an apologetic and rather awkward expression: "Sorry, Alice’s thought process is sometimes unconventional..."
At this point, it seemed Lei Nora had just recovered from the shock, staring blankly at Duncan for a moment before finally saying, "...This is my first time seeing this scene from a third-person perspective."
Duncan: "..."
But what surprised him even more was the Frost Queen’s second sentence: "Honestly, it’s quite amusing."
Duncan was dumbfounded and after a long pause he managed to respond, "... You’re really broad-minded."
"I was chatting with Alice when I heard her mention that her neck joint tends to loosen easily, so I curiously asked her what exactly she meant," Lei Nora spread her hands, her expression much more Calmness than before, "Of course, her way of demonstrating was indeed a bit more thrilling than I had anticipated..."
What could Duncan say? He could only twitch the corners of his mouth and turn his head to look at the humanoid automaton—who was walking over while adjusting the angle of her head without realizing the mood was a bit delicate—and she bent over directly in front of Duncan, presenting her neck: "Captain, there’s a hair clip caught in the joint, help me get it out."
Duncan’s eye corner twitched, and with an awkward expression, he started to disentangle the hair from Alice’s neck joint while giving Lei Nora an embarrassed smile.
Lei Nora, however, seemed unconcerned, her interest piqued as she watched this scene—which was far removed from "simple and normal life" yet somehow strangely peaceful—before she finally laughed and said, "It seems she does live quite happily."
"It’d be better if she didn’t always lack worries like this," Duncan sighed helplessly, "Seriously, are you okay? About that scene just now... I thought you might be traumatized..."
"I’m fine," Lei Nora took a breath, "Back when it was cut off, I didn’t see it myself—imaginary issues can be overcome."
Duncan thought about it and realized that this "Frost Queen" obviously had a very strong inner strength—and even stronger peripheral nerves.
At this moment, Alice also seemed to realize something, turning her head to Duncan: "Captain, are you here to find me?"
"Yes," Duncan carefully freed the last strand of hair stuck in the joint and nodded, "We have arrived here, and there’s an appointment... it’s time to honor it."
Alice blinked, finally remembering something, "Ah, that flaming meatball hanging at the door..."
Duncan was somewhat surprised; he was astonished that the automaton could accurately remember this matter but was even more impressed by Alice’s refreshingly unconventional description.
Lei Nora, clueless on the side, watched them without understanding what they were talking about, and couldn’t help asking curiously, "An appointment? Where are we heading next?"
"It’s an appointment for Alice and me," Duncan said with a smile, "Don’t worry, we won’t leave this ship, we’re just going to briefly visit another dimension, we’ll be back soon."
"Right, the captain is going to wind me up!" Alice also said happily, waving to Lei Nora, "You go back to your room first, I’ll come to play with you after I’m wound up!"
Lei Nora listened and was even more bewildered: "Wind you up?"
But the automaton apparently had no intention of further explaining and was already tugging the captain towards the rear deck, both of them walking away quickly.
Leaving the "Frost Queen" standing there with a face full of confusion, her mind brimming with question marks.

chapters.title: Chapter 844 - 841: Faith
chapters.content:
Chapter 844: Chapter 841: Faith
Not long into this world-ending journey, Duncan had made a covenant with that revolution of the Black Sun—after he reached the frontier of order and confirmed the cornerstone of the new world, he was to answer the latter’s request for a place in the new world. At that time, the Black Sun would also show him a "clue" related to the new world.
Now, Homeloss had arrived at the Endless Sea, and the time had come to honor the appointment.
In the depths of the captain’s quarters, Alice sat obediently with her back to Duncan on the bed, the navigational key smoothly slid into the keyhole of the doll and began to turn on its own with a slight friction noise—after the familiar slight dizziness and perception reset, Duncan found himself in the spacious and ornate, yet exceptionally eerie hall of Alice’s Mansion.
The dim-colored mansion door, covered with intricate patterns, stood silently at the end of the carpet, with faint sunlight seemingly fluttering through the gaps; the shadow of the Black Sun must still be waiting outside the door.
However, Duncan did not directly go outside to meet the appointment; instead, he first turned to walk deeper into the mansion—he found Alice, lost in thought with a drawing board, in the navigation chamber before bringing the doll back to the hall, up to the mansion door.
For some reason, he hoped that the doll would witness alongside him everything that he would experience in this "Place of the End of All Things".
Alice, for her part, didn’t think too much of it. She was simply happy, as happy as she was every day. She seemed very much looking forward to meeting that "burning meatball," and as a "high-order anomaly" who hadn’t lived much in human society, she did not seem to fear the Black Sun nor show any aversion to the dangerous "old god".
Duncan arrived in front of the mansion door and, just like last time, pushed open the slightly ajar heavy door effortlessly—as the hinges squeaked and creaked, the seemingly weighty but in fact seemingly weightless doors swung open, and the bright, dazzling yet not scorching false sunlight rushed towards him, gloriously filling his view.
Within a bright shell of flames, the pale and deformed mass of flesh slowly expanded and writhed, and the massive eye was half-open as if casting a glance from a dream: "Ah, Usurper of Flame, you have appeared... have you come to answer my call?"
Duncan faced the oncoming sunlight: "I have now reached the end of all things and confirmed the matters regarding the cornerstone of the new world. I am here to meet you, as per our agreement."
The flesh inside the Black Sun appeared to stir slightly, and its outer flames gently rose, with a sonorous tremble voicing from in-between the countless tendrils and swellings: "Ah, it sounds like you have made great progress... so, about my initial request, for a place in the new world..."
"Agreed," Duncan cut off the other party’s speech simply and straightforwardly.
Perhaps because this answer came too readily, the Black Sun seemed stunned for a moment. Its flesh movement and trembling sound paused for a few seconds before hesitantly uttering again: "Are you certain...?"
"Yes, the new world is vast, big enough to give you—and the memory of your ’homeland’—a place," Duncan spoke earnestly, "but only if the new world can be completed as planned."
"...You’re not worried that I’ll become a ’dangerous element’ in the new world?" The Black Sun now seemed puzzled, "My race and I have been exiled by the Shelter for ten thousand years, and you are trying to bring me and the other races from the Shelter to the new world. Aren’t you concerned this might be a hidden danger?"
"I’ve said it before, the new world is vast," Duncan remained calm as he reiterated, "so vast—your civilization is not an immortal species, and the ’hidden danger’ you speak of will be dissipated in the grand scale of space and the accompanying temporal scale, ensuring a sufficiently safe period during which your civilization will have no opportunity to make contact with others. As for you..."
Duncan paused, a hint of a smile appearing at the bottom of his eyes.
"As one of the ’Ancient Kings’ at the founding of the Shelter, you are well-versed in the Primordial Blueprint of the Endless Sea and all its system flaws. Considering your demonstrated understanding of the ’Shelter,’ I guess... this world never actually had the ability to ’exile’ you, or to put it another way—if you wanted to return to the Endless Sea, you would have returned on the day when the Ancient Crete Kingdom elevated Anomaly 001 into the sky."
He looked up, quietly gazing into the massive eye at the heart of the writhing sun.
"During the construction of this Shelter, there is no record of warfare between the Ancient Kings, everything was the result of negotiations—you chose to be exiled voluntarily. It’s just that the offspring and remnants that sprouted from you... let things spiral out of control."
The Black Sun fell silent for a moment, before finally slowly speaking: "The building of the Shelter was very ’extreme,’ at that time there wasn’t even a trace of spare resources or time to waste, the Long Night had failed twice, and we had to succeed on the third... No one had a choice."
"Thank you for your rationality back then, so let’s forego meaningless probing and assumptions. Regarding the new world, I have my own arrangements—now it’s your turn to fulfill your promise," Duncan’s tone shifted, his expression growing serious, "you claimed you had ’evidence’ about the new world, what exactly is that?"
The Black Sun did not speak, but slowly stretched out its delicate tendrils from the edge of the solar corona. Along the edge of the burning false corona, a limb suddenly extended—seemingly wrapped around something, it spanned the vast distance and was accurately passed in front of Duncan.
Eli, who had been daydreaming beside him, was startled and immediately came up curiously: "What is this?"
"A letter," echoed the layered trembling voice of the Black Sun in the emptiness, then the "delicate" tendril spread slowly, revealing an object in Duncan’s view.
It was merely a silver-gray cube, resembling a metal ingot, about ten centimeters on a side, with what appeared to be patterns etched onto the surface. While the design was curious, it did not seem as significant as Duncan had initially thought.
He looked at the small metal cube with bewilderment, noticing its surface had a faint translucent and blurry texture—considering that only the Black Sun’s projection had come here, it was clear that the cube shown was also merely a projection.
The essence of this cube should reside together with the Black Sun, somewhere beyond the reality dimension.
Duncan suddenly frowned as he noticed certain patterns on the surface of the cube.
The Black Sun seemingly anticipated this; as Duncan’s gaze changed, it thoughtfully projected the cube before him and slowly rotated it, displaying every side.
Duncan saw the silhouette of a human figure, standing on a coordinate diagram filled with various markings and reference points.
On the second surface, he saw an array of circles, arranged from small to large.
On the third surface, there were intersecting lines, the intersections of which seemed to demonstrate some kind of mathematical law.
On the fourth surface, however, was a child-like, scrawling drawing, crude compared to the precise and seemingly meaningful patterns on the previous sides.
The fifth surface bore countless seemingly-random indentations, resembling a star chart of a constellation or a similar celestial system.
Duncan shifted his gaze to the sixth surface.
It was covered in distorted symbols!
They appeared to be various kinds of writing initially, but under the influence of some force, all the text—or the information they represented—had been twisted into shapes utterly unrecognizable. Duncan even felt as though these distorted symbols were alive; as he stared at them, every single line trembled and reconfigured on its own, making it impossible to discern their true contours.
Subconsciously, Duncan reached out towards the cube, but his fingers simply passed through the illusion.
The voice of the Black Sun reached his ears: "Its ’physical’ form is not here, but I can describe its state to you—
"It is a metal ingot with the hardness of steel yet surprisingly light; it is hollow inside, concealing a powerful source of energy, and I cannot inspect its internal structure in detail without damaging its integrity; it seems to possess some sort of powerful ’mechanism’ that releases information, which also lies hidden within.
"There’s one more thing: It seems that it originally carried even more information, including those ’writings’ you noticed that can no longer be read, and this ’information’ is inaccessible.
"At first, it even emitted sounds, but those were just chaotic noise; it continuously released some sort of ’signal,’ but even I cannot understand what it is, and now, its release process has all but ceased—I cannot tell if it’s due to a malfunction or energy depletion... but it probably isn’t about energy, because up to this moment, the energy reaction inside it remains strong."
Listened to the Black Sun’s narrative, Duncan fell silent for a long time, simply staring at the continually rotating cube before finally breaking the silence, "So, this is a letter, a letter sent from the ’New World’ to the ’Old World’—is that what you mean?"
"Yes."
"But how can we be sure?" Duncan couldn’t help asking, "How do you know it’s not just another relic from the Great Annihilation? Like the other twisted fragments."
"Because it comes from a place where, theoretically, no ’fragments’ could exist," said the Black Sun calmly.
Duncan immediately frowned, "A place where no fragments could exist?"
"...Creation of the World."
There was an instant silence at the scene.
Duncan’s eyes widened slightly in astonishment as he stared at the projection of the cube, at every surface that strove to convey various pieces of information, and at the erased text.
This is a letter.
However, who dispatched this letter...?
(Book recommendation! From Yan ZK, "Summoning the World to Death," an engaging Eastern fantasy epic by a top author. Interested readers may want to check it out!)

chapters.title: Chapter 845 - 842: A Well-thought-out Alternative Plan
chapters.content:
Chapter 845: Chapter 842: A Well-thought-out Alternative Plan
Duncan gazed intently at the cube floating at the end of Black Sun’s tendril, at the symbols on its surface that seemed to have exhausted every effort to convey their message to him.
He imagined how such a small metallic block could have been delivered to this world—delivered to this era—what method, what process it had undergone.
It was a letter, a message from the New World to the Old World. Yet, all evidence proving this had been erased by some force. Its creator might have tried countless ways to ensure that the cube could "reveal its origin," but it seemed that these efforts were unsuccessful—though unsuccessful did not mean meaningless.
The very appearance of it was a kind of interpretation, although this interpretation appeared to be a wildly bold conjecture by Black Sun. At this moment, Duncan was more than willing to believe that this conjecture was the one and only correct answer.
In the midst of this silence, the deep, layered tremor of Black Sun finally broke the quiet: "The manufacturing techniques and operational methods of this cube exceed my understanding—exceed the knowledge systems of any City-State that have existed now or in the past, and surpass any technology known to me from before the Great Oblivion."
"On the other hand, considering ’purpose,’ I can find no reason why anyone would make and place the cube inside the Creation of the World—let alone that even the ancient kings’ powers could not manage to send something into the Creation of the World. Hence, the only explanation I can think of is that this cube comes from a world and era beyond my comprehension.
"I am familiar with all the history of this Shelter—the only history I do not understand is the future.
"The future concerning the ’New World.’
The brilliant yet false corona at the edge of Black Sun slowly unfolded, its tendrils, scorched by fierce flames, stretched out in the sea of fire and slowly curled again.
And the tendril that stretched a vast distance, reaching the entrance of the mansion, steadily remained before Duncan, as if holding some precious treasure, carefully supporting the unremarkable-looking, small, metallic cube.
"Usurper of the Flame, this letter has no recipient. Someone or some people from the New World tried every means to send it to this era, but they couldn’t ensure that the cube would reach someone’s hands accurately... However, I have a feeling that it was meant for you."
Duncan found it hard to articulate his feelings at the moment. He looked at the symbols and patterns on the surface of the cube; although all the inscriptions were blurred and chaotic, he still grasped a part of the message the "letter" conveyed—
The human body (self), principles, mathematics, a child’s doodles, and stars.
"They live in a rational and stable world... They can see the stars," Duncan murmured to himself as if talking to the air, "They live safely, and..."
"And, they have reached a very high stage of development," Black Sun slowly added. "The manufacturing technique used for this cube is beyond belief, and so is the method employed to send it ’here.’ It is something that has never appeared in any ’blueprints.’"
Duncan didn’t speak for a while. Alice, standing by his side, blinked curiously. The doll-like lady looked at the distant Black Sun, then at the nearby cube. Although she didn’t understand complex and profound issues like "manufacturing techniques," "developmental stages," or "blueprints," she at least grasped that the cube was something important sent by someone, making her unable to hold back her curiosity and break the silence: "Captain, who could have sent this ’letter’?"
Someone or some people from the New World.
That answer emerged first in Duncan’s mind, but he hesitated to speak it out loud. After a long reflection, he reached out tentatively towards the phantom-like cube—a cluster of starlight-flecked flames leaped at his fingertips.
Black Sun’s tendril instinctively recoiled as the flame neared but eventually stretched out again, softly reminding, "This is only its illusion; the actual cube is not here."
"I know, I just want to try to ’hear’ or ’see’ something," said Duncan, "Illusion or reality doesn’t matter to me; as long as there is a connection of information, that’s enough."
Black Sun said no more, but slightly lifted the cube’s illusion on its tendril.
The flame at Duncan’s fingertips silently merged into the illusion, like rain dissolving into water.
He remained silent, intently sensing the information passed on by the flame—he felt how the flame gradually faded in the void, but even with the eyes of a Reverse Singularity, he saw nothing deep within the fire.
No echo, no "memory." It seemed that all the deep information carried by the cube had been obliterated in the process of passing through the Creation of the World.
Duncan patiently waited for a long time, until the last trace of flame completely dissipated in the depths of the illusion. Nothing responded to him; only emptiness lay deep within the cube.
Alice watched wide-eyed by his side, silent the whole time for fear of causing trouble, until she saw the captain let out a slight sigh. She couldn’t help but move closer: "Did you see anything?"
"Nothing," Duncan gently shook his head, "I’m afraid it’s all been eroded clean during the ’transfer’ process."
Alice looked stunned, disappointment surfacing on her face: "...Oh."
Duncan felt the same disappointment but said nothing more, just waved his hand lightly, withdrawing his gaze from the metallic cube.
However, just as he averted his eyes, as if a wisp of an incredibly ethereal breeze blew by, a phantom-like flicker crossed his mind—during that nearly hallucinatory instant, he heard a voice, as though emerging directly from his memory:
"...I will do everything in my power to see you again... I must find a way to leave something behind..."
Duncan turned sharply, staring intently at the small cube.
The sound at that instant was so ethereal and elusive that he couldn’t even be sure if it had any connection with the cubic artifact, or if it was merely a "memory" that had popped up in his mind. The voice did not appear again, everything seemed like his own hallucination.
But a few seconds later, a slight smile suddenly appeared on his face.
In his mind emerged the figure of a hunched, elderly Cretan elder in a worn white robe—the old man who walked into the twilight of the world’s end, waving goodbye without looking back, stepping into the endless night with almost no guidance, in search of the slim glimmer that should not have been able to shine upon the old world.
The Cretan elder had succeeded.
He had sent a message of peace from the new world.
...And perhaps it wasn’t just a "status update" message.
Duncan seemed to think of something, his brow furrowed in deep thought, his expressions changing — Alice, perceptive to the changes in the ship captain, felt a tinge of worry and couldn’t help but step forward and tug at Duncan’s sleeve: "Captain?"
Duncan raised his head with a still solemn expression, and casually patted the Puppet Lady’s hair, looking at the distant Black Sun: "You just said that this cubic artifact came ’from’ the Creation of the World?"
"Yes," Black Sun immediately answered, "This cubic artifact has ’surfaced’ from the depths of the Creation of the World, that much I can be certain of."
"It sounds like you know quite a bit about the Creation of the World and have always been keeping an eye on it," Duncan’s expression turned serious, "Other ’Ancient Kings’ don’t seem to know as much about it as you."
"As you said," the imposing eye faced Duncan squarely without concealment, "I know many things related to the Creation of the World, just as I understand the entire Endless Sea... Do you remember what I said at the beginning? Throughout the long years, I’ve been ’overlooking’ this world..."
Upon hearing Black Sun’s words, Duncan’s face changed slightly, then he suddenly realized: "Wait, are you saying... your true body is actually inside the Creation of the World?!"
"No, I am on its ’reverse side’," Black Sun said calmly, "No one can stay within the Creation of the World, not even the so-called ’Ancient Kings’; it is a place that devours and tears apart everything, it is the end of the world itself—but apart from that, the Creation of the World itself... is an impregnable ’barrier’."
"It is sufficient to completely separate the entire Endless Sea and those harmful, dangerous exiles, shielding the toxic, corrosive ’influences’ to the Shelter on the other side of the barrier—at the ’reverse side’ of the Creation of the World, lies the cold land of exile, and for ten thousand years, I’ve been right here, just above everyone’s heads."
The... reverse side of the Creation of the World!
Duncan felt his heart pound. A reality he had always ignored suddenly came before his eyes—the Creation of the World actually had a "reverse side," and on that unbelievable "reverse side," Black Sun, the most ancient and dangerous "ancient god" that terrorized the whole world, was actually suspended above the heads of mortal beings?!
After a brief shock, Duncan suddenly realized something—
Why the cubic artifact that "passed through" the Creation of the World and was sent to this era fell into Black Sun’s hands—because in this world, the one closest to the Creation of the World is this ancient god, exiled ten thousand years ago!
"Usurper of Fire," at this moment, Black Sun’s voice came, interrupting Duncan’s thoughts, "Why are you suddenly interested in the Creation of the World?"
Duncan immediately collected his scattered thoughts. After briefly composing himself, he looked up earnestly at the ancient "deity".
"I have a rather bold plan... It might sound a bit insane."
"Oh?" Black Sun made a curious sound, "Can you tell me? Is it related to the Creation of the World?"
Duncan thought for a moment and nodded earnestly: "Simply put, I plan to detonate it."
Black Sun went silent in an instant.
After an unknowable length of time, the twisted and indescribable "ancient god" suddenly emitted a series of strange tremors and gurgling sounds from within, and then the disordered noise reassembled into a coherent syllable—
"...Huh?"
(Of course, before the book’s end, I have to quickly... plug a few books to pad it out! This time I am recommending "Sword Path Ashes," by the author Panda Who Wrestles, who is also a reader of mine. Below is his own introduction:)
After Xie Xuanyi fell into the North Sea, under the nurturing of the Fountain of Immortality, he unexpectedly welcomed his second life.
Enchantress, Sword Immortal, Buddha’s Son... with demons dancing wildly and a great tide approaching, another golden age has arrived!
In his previous life, his body was feeble; this life, he forged Lustrous Vajra Bones with golden Vital Energy!
The three hundred flying swords of the past all broke, so he refined an entire realm of sword qi!
Milk for the Sky Sacrifice.)

chapters.title: Chapter 846 - 843: Leading Light
chapters.content:
Chapter 846: Chapter 843: Leading Light
Duncan felt that his plan might indeed be a bit crazy—the Black Sun probably just failed a sanity check upon hearing what he just said...
But he was serious. After the Black Sun uttered an "ah", his expression became even more solemn than before, and he calmly repeated, "I want to detonate the Creation of the World—of course, this ’detonation’ is a figurative term. Strictly speaking, I want to utilize its power, or rather, the part of its power that wasn’t fully released during the great annihilation."
The surface of the false burning sun swelled and fluctuated, the dazzling corona rose up like lofty waves and storms, and countless pale, bizarre tentacles writhed and coiled in the sea of fire. After a while, the Black Sun calmed down, and its deep, tremulous voice gained some noise: "...When did you decide on this plan?"
"Before I came to see you," Duncan said calmly, "although at that time it was just a vague direction and the thought was not so firm."
He paused briefly, then continued: "I have always had an ... ’Intuition’. This intuition may stem from the ’knowledge’ left by the civilization that created me. I don’t understand the internal principles of many things, but instinct tells me how to proceed or where the direction lies. It was under the drive of this intuition that I thought the Creation of the World might help me solve a major problem I currently face—the problem of the First Mover."
"But it was not until I met you here and saw the ’letter’ you brought to me, that I confirmed the correctness of this direction, or rather... this letter itself is most likely a reminder, reminding me where the correct direction lies."
The restless undulation on the surface of the Black Sun softened slightly upon realizing that this was not a mindless mad idea, but actually a calm and rational plan; it finally turned serious: "What do you mean by ’the problem of the First Mover’ that you just mentioned?"
"Simply put, it is the ’Big Bang’ that prompted the birth of the world," Duncan explained, "This is a more figurative expression. You could consider it as a synchronous explosion of information, matter, and energy. If we view the entire world as a massive and complex mathematical machine, then the very first roar of this mathematical machine is that ’explosion’ marking the genesis of everything."
"In the ashes of the edge of order, I conducted preliminary tests. These tests validated the hypothesis of information immortality and confirmed that by ’assignment’, it is indeed possible to Reshape everything in the chaotic Sea of Information. However, I discovered another issue— this ’mathematical machine’ of the world has ’integrity’; all its information parameters must mesh together. I can’t rebuild the world brick by brick, step by step like building a house—Before this process begins, I might have an endless amount of time to prepare, but once it starts, all tasks must be completed synchronously."
"Therefore, I need such an explosion, in an infinitely brief yet enduring ’instant’, to accomplish a synchronous assignment and ’activation’ of all information. If this condition isn’t met, the new world would be torn apart and gradually reset to zero—just like the current Endless Sea."
"And this requires an enormous amount of energy, an extremely enormous amount... even energy on the scale of the great annihilation."
Duncan raised his head, looking seriously at the massive, pallid eye surrounded by flesh: "You see, this is a rather reasonable and well-considered plan..."
"...I’m starting to get a little scared whenever you mention ’reasonable’," the tentacles around the Black Sun tremored, "But okay, I at least understand the necessity of this plan, indeed... such enormous energy, only the Creation of the World can provide. But how will you ensure this process... really will happen as you imagine? To put it directly, how should the Creation of the World be detonated? How to guide it? How to ensure this process doesn’t go out of control?"
This ancient god threw a series of questions, obviously having great concerns about Duncan’s plan—which are indeed normal.
Because it was too close to the Creation of the World; no "person" on this world knows the nature and terror of that rift better than it, as it has been staring at the doom frozen in the sky for ten thousand years—this makes it very difficult for it to associate that doom with a "new world."
Duncan had clearly thought through these questions as well. Facing the doubts from the Black Sun, he showed no wavering and simply organized his thoughts briefly before calmly speaking: "Everything is Information."
The Black Sun fell silent, waiting for Duncan to continue explaining.
"The Creation of the World is no exception," Duncan promptly added.
The flames around the Black Sun contracted for a moment; it seemed to have thought of something.
"Having come into contact with that chaotic state of the ’Sea of Information’, I’ve truly comprehended the theory of ’Everything is Information’," Duncan didn’t play any mysteries, and after confirming the Black Sun could follow his thoughts, he continued to explain, "The Creation of the World is the solidified ’doom’ itself, yet doom is also a form of information expression. From the most fundamental logic, the Creation of the World is essentially no different from anything else in this world.
"For me, as long as it is still supported by ’information’, there is no issue of it being ’out of control’. It exists; it is controllable. If it’s uncontrollable... then its ’uncontrollability’ must also be controllable, unless the theory of ’Everything is Information’ no longer applies to it."
"You sound very confident," the tentacles of the Black Sun stretched out, noting with a deep and gentle tremor, "and very firm."
Duncan didn’t say anything but simply nodded lightly.
He truly believed so: nothing could stop the Creation of the World from becoming the dawn of the new world—not even the Creation of the World itself.
"Moreover, another thing also strengthens my belief," he suddenly stated.
Black Sun quickly responded, "Are you talking about... the appearance of that cube?"
"It passed through the rift of Creation of the World and arrived ’on this side’," Duncan nodded gently, "A letter, no matter how exquisitely it is crafted, or how complete its protective measures are, the fact that it could travel between the old world and the new world and be delivered ’here’ is almost impossible in itself. Therefore, its ’delivery window’ must be carefully chosen - that window surely lies at the place where the two worlds ’connect’ most tightly..."
Duncan slowly halted, his gaze drifting towards the horizon, as though looking through the brilliant but spurious corona of Black Sun, gazing at some even more distant time-space––
The old world’s everything collapses, all information ultimately converges at an "end point";
The new world is born from a massive eruption, all information bursting forth from a "starting point".
Convergence and explosion, born relative to each other, like the two ends of an hourglass, and at their junction—the place that is both the end point and the starting point—is the location left for "Reverse Singularity".
It is also the location left for Creation of the World.
The people of the distant future, send a letter through that one and only "aperture" to the other end of the hourglass. The letter is a family message of well-being, and also a lamp leading the way during a night sail.
"I will go find you," Duncan slowly said, retracting his gaze from the distance, focusing once again on Black Sun, "I will fulfill the promise to incinerate you, reserve a place for you in the new world, and then—the matter will be done."
The corona of Black Sun undulated slowly, and from within those layers of flesh, came a gentle and deep trembling voice: "I will light a lighthouse for you, in the night sky, steer towards the brightest direction."
"Alright, see you then."
"See you then."
...
Night eternally veils the City-State, with fog enveloping, and frozen clouds hanging seemingly within reach, cold permeates the world, street gas lamps arranged neatly still shining brightly, yet the flames within the lamps frozen, emitting not a hint of heat.
Heidi wrapped herself tightly in her coat—although she wasn’t sure why she had to wear such warm clothes, something instinctual within her decided to "keep warm," even though she could barely remember what "cold" meant anymore.
She hurried along the streets lit by streetlights, showing her pass at the constable’s post and continued towards home.
On the streets, there were sparse passersby, some heading to factories, others out shopping; compared to the early days of the prolonged night, there were visibly more people out and about now—it seemed as though over time, the people of the City-State had gradually adapted to this endless night.
But even so, compared to those "business as usual" days of the past, the city was still much too silent.
Heidi paid no heed to those slowly moving figures in the fog, just hurriedly walked on. Occasionally, she heard some commotion or fear-stricken screams from street corners or neighboring blocks—sometimes even witnessing fully armed church guards clashing with panicking pedestrians in the fog, but she quickly diverted her eyes, ignoring these matters.
As she passed a streetlight, Heidi looked up and caught a glimpse in the corner of her eye of a flyer stuck to the lamp post, the flyer hosting simple phrases—
"Waves, death, the temperature of fire—if you see and understand these words, please proceed immediately to the shelter in XX district or XX district. Do not panic, stay calm, you are still being protected."
Heidi frowned, looking at those crooked, indecipherable symbols.
She faintly felt that she had often seen such graffiti around her neighborhood recently.
But there was nothing worth noting in that.
She turned her head, crossed through the cold fog, and continued toward home.

chapters.title: Chapter 847 - 844: Going Home
chapters.content:
Chapter 847: Chapter 844: Going Home
Slight dizziness and a subtle sense of discomfort once again permeated the air at the last intersection on the way home. Heidi paused, puzzled, and looked back in the direction she had come from.
A thin mist blanketed the street, clouds hung low over the rooftops, and the streetlights emitted a cold, dim glow. Some vague, shaky shadows fluctuated in the mist, occasionally emitting incomprehensible, dream-like chaotic noises, but nothing seemed out of the ordinary.
She furrowed her brow, catching a glimpse from the corner of her eye of some text carved into the wall beside her, the crooked symbols there giving her a headache.
Not far from the street, a robust woman stood at a doorway. Perhaps noticing Heidi, who was dazed in the middle of the road, the lady looked on with curiosity, "Good evening, do you need help?"
"...No," Heidi hesitated before responding, "I’m fine, just a bit dizzy."
"You should take care of yourself, dizziness is no small matter," the robust lady said with a friendly smile, "If you’re feeling unwell, you can come in and take a seat. I have some hot tea."
Aware of the other’s genuine kindness, Heidi smiled and waved her hand: "Thank you for your kindness, but I’m feeling much better now."
"Is that so? It seems that breathing in some fresh air indeed helps. It’s good weather today..."
Heidi nodded, politely thanked her and then withdrew her gaze. Shortly after that, she saw a stranger in a blue coat approaching through the mist, the man carrying what appeared to be a heavy parcel, hurrying along, with a look of fear in his eyes—as if something terrible chased him through the mist, making him glance around anxiously while walking yet dared not make any sudden moves, as if afraid of disturbing something in the mist.
Heidi unconsciously scrunched her brow and approached the anxious man: "Hello, sir, are you in trouble? I am a psychiatrist..."
The man in the blue coat jumped in shock, stopped in his tracks and stared wide-eyed at Heidi, his mouth opening as if he wanted to speak, but then he seemed to notice something on Heidi, his eyes suddenly filled with intense wariness and almost rudely waved his hand before turning and walking deeper into the mist without saying a word.
Heidi furrowed her brows in confusion, looked down at herself, sensing nothing unpleasant about her appearance.
That slight dizziness and subtle sense of discomfort once again intensified.
A sense of vigilance quietly rose in Heidi’s heart, although she did not know what she should be wary of. But her long-dormant psychic senses seemed suddenly to awaken, and she began to sense danger and coldness in the seemingly ordinary streets around her.
Something... was off, within her line of sight, all around her, but she had overlooked them... those discordant things...
Heidi quietly moved to the edge of the sidewalk, cautiously observing her surroundings while silently invoking the name of Rahm. Her hand hung low, and a sharp golden spike silently slipped into her grip.
But she did not know what this golden spike could be used against... Was there really an enemy?
The pendant on her chest emitted a slight warmth, as if reminding her of something.
Heidi’s gaze swept past her side; those ’graffiti’ unknowingly carved on the wall caught her eyes again, their twisted lines wriggling, quivering, suddenly forming readable shapes: "Waves, death, the temperature of fire..."
Heidi abruptly froze.
The howling of reason and memory surged like the once ignored waves, coming upon her inevitably like death, she began to understand, to perceive, to recognize the changes that had occurred in this world, and the panic that had been suppressed for an unknown length of time nearly knocked her over in the first second—but years of mental training allowed her to steady her steps, maintaining sanity and courage faster than anyone, and she looked up at her surroundings.
Flesh-like dark red shadows spread in the night, covering all the walls and rooftops around, clouds hung as if another land crushing down from above, the cold light of Creation of the World shone through the clouds, turning into indistinct, bizarre, and trembling shadows, licking and drifting around the city sky as if alive, and in the mist-covered street, the confused human silhouettes swayed like zombies, emitting low murmurs and whimpers.
A man in a gray coat approached, holding a rotten and suspicious substance, muttering to himself while stuffing it into his mouth.
A bicycle with no one controlling it slowly moved along the street, its decayed wheels and chain making a creaking noise, with only a silhouette the size of a human head on the saddle.
A giant limb of flesh crawled out of a nearby house, the thousands of eyes at the edge of the limb blinking in the fog. The terrifying piece of flesh turned around, those eyes erratically looking in every direction in the cold night, yet human-like voices emanated from the flesh:
"Good evening... It is good weather today..."
Heidi gasped, a chill deep enough to freeze her heart and lungs steeped deep into her blood.
Suddenly, she remembered the graffiti and carvings that had appeared daily on the streets, the inexplicable discordance she had felt, and that hurried, frightened man in the blue coat.
She remembered her mother, still at home!
She sharply inhaled, turned, and sprinted towards the foggy street, running home as fast as she could—
It seemed like someone was whispering in fear through the fog, someone far away seemed to be shouting her name, the dark red shadows on both sides of the road, squirming and trembling like flesh, gathered together in a disgusting manner then slowly separated to both sides, gunshots came from the next block, seemingly someone had caused a disturbance in fear, a steam-powered walking machine with many eyes and mouths came staggering from the opposite side, its pressure pipes split open, humming an odd, monotonous melody.
Heidi appeared to neither hear nor see any of these; she shielded all distractions to the side, simply focusing on running straight down the street—crossing through the thin mist until the light at her doorstep finally faintly appeared in her view.
She grabbed her long skirt, running the last few meters ungracefully, but she paused for a moment before opening the door. Hesitating, she transferred the sharp "Golden Spike" to her left hand, adjusted her breathing, and then cautiously took out her keys, unlocked the door, and turned the handle.
The door opened, and the cold, bright light of the living room shone into her eyes. Everything in the house seemed as usual—the corners of the walls still vaguely showed some squirming shadows, but at least it was many times more "normal" than the streets outside.
Her mother sat by the fireplace at the end of the living room, seemingly engrossed in reading a newspaper that had come at some unknown time.
Upon hearing the door open, the old woman by the fireplace lifted her head, revealing a gentle smile: "Heidi, you’re back—was the house call successful?"
Her mother looked the same as usual, and the room had no "intruders" as she had feared.
Heidi quietly breathed a sigh of relief, put away the Golden Spike, then quickly walked towards the fireplace: "There’s no time to explain, mother, you need to come with me now, we need to leave this place, this block is not safe, there’s something outside..."
As she spoke, she hesitated and stopped.
Because her mother’s face still wore a gentle smile, with no trace of surprise or question—after Heidi hesitated and stopped, the old woman nodded then stood up and walked to the stairs on the other side of the fireplace.
She took two suitcases out from under the stairs.
"Everything essential is in here, the Shelter has basic amenities, and the supplies are fairly sufficient—Dante Wayne always does a good job.
"Your ’medical box’ is also packed, placed on the table in your room, you get it yourself, it will still be needed at the Shelter.
"Take your revolver, bring a few extra boxes of bullets—try not to use them, but if you must, shoot accurately, the bullets are still effective against those fleshly, crawling things."
The old woman spoke while coming back in front of the fireplace, she stood on tiptoe slightly, with some effort, took down the old rifle hanging on the brass hook.
Click, click, the old woman skillfully checked the gun’s mechanism, pushed the bullets into the chamber, then withdrew and reloaded them.
"This will do for me, it’s the same one I used when accompanying your father on trips, this old chap is very reliable, a Heretic per bullet."
Heidi watched this scene dumbfounded, only to gradually come to her senses, incredulously looking at her mother: "Mother, you’ve already..."
"They had been prepared since the first time they posted flyers on the lampposts, and since then the days were just about waiting for you to ’wake’ up," the old woman looked up at Heidi, "fortunately, we didn’t have to wait too long."
Heidi was speechless in shock for a long time, until her mother began to urge her, then she finally snapped out of it, hurriedly agreeing and running upstairs to her room—she found the neatly arranged small suitcase and several cardboard boxes on the table prepared by her mother.
She opened the box, inside were shiny golden bullets—each bullet head was stamped with the sacred sayings of the God of Wisdom Rahm in special ink:
"Let knowledge enter into the mind."
Heidi looked at those golden bullets, steadied herself, hid some of the bullets in several pockets on her body, the rest she carefully wrapped and placed in the medical box.
After finishing all this, she turned and quickly ran down the stairs.
"Mother, I’m ready, let’s..."
Heidi suddenly stopped on the stairs.
She saw the door of the house wide open, a familiar figure standing at the entrance.
Wearing an old but clean and tidy woollen coat, with a monocular eyeglass, and chewing on a pipe.
Father was home.

chapters.title: Chapter 848 - 845: The Final Voyage Plan
chapters.content:
Chapter 848: Chapter 845: The Final Voyage Plan
After bringing all the new luggage to the living room, Heidi went to the dining table and looked absent-mindedly at Maurice sitting across from her.
She hadn’t seen her father for a long time—although they could still occasionally get in touch, but even that intermittent contact seemed to have been a thing of the past.
Her father’s sudden return home felt like a dream to her, unreal.
Maurice sat at the dining table, unhurriedly eating the freshly fried sausages and bread, chewing each bite thoroughly. After a while, he looked up at his wife sitting beside him and his daughter across the table, with a smile on his face: "I haven’t had home-cooked food in a long time."
"There’s more if you’re still hungry, but after this meal, we need to go out," his wife said with a smile, as if it was like the old days when the couple would discuss taking a walk in the park after lunch, "We are heading to the nearest shelter to check in—the neighborhood is getting more and more unsettled, those bewildered people... are looking less and less human."
"They’ve lost their self-awareness, and this world is also gradually forgetting what ’humans’ look like, resulting in them becoming like that," Maurice said calmly, "The keystones and anchors laid down by the gods are quickly losing effectiveness, and those who haven’t awakened will drift further from ’normal’ over time... yet in their own ’feeling,’ nothing has ever changed."
Heidi’s face showed a hint of sorrow: "...Is there no hope left?"
"Don’t worry about them, Heidi," her father simply smiled and shook his head across the table, "It’s all temporary, things will get better. The captain is working out a plan—I’ve returned to the City-State early as part of his grand scheme."
"...It seems you’ve been through a lot outside," Heidi hesitated before speaking out, "Has everyone else returned too? Has Fenna come back?"
"Yes, Fenna has returned. Except for the captain, Alice, and that pigeon, the rest of the ’crew’ have returned home," Maurice nodded slowly, "Fenna has gone to the cathedral, and then she will head to the town hall. After settling the matters there, she will contact you. Nina and Sherry have also returned home; we’ve set up a time and method for contact, and the sailors and Agatha... they all have their own arrangements and missions."
Heidi’s face showed a hint of curiosity: "...Can you tell me about your journey?"
"Of course—there’s not much world time left, but still enough for a grand and tumultuous tale."
Amidst the mist that shrouded the city, the figures of two girls ran through the streets of the Lower City District.
They passed through intersections piled with suspicious dark-red lumps, moved between buildings that seemed to blink countless eyes and had walls that undulated, bypassed aimless, unaware shadows wandering the streets; the low murmurs and occasional bursts of noise emanated from the mist, as if chasing uninvited guests, circling around them.
"This is even worse than what the Female Pope described!" Sherry felt the atmosphere around her creepily unnerving. To embolden herself, she transformed into a horrifying demon with twelve long skeletal limbs, carefully stepping over the pulsating piles on the ground, "She only mentioned that the city is full of people who have lost themselves... but she didn’t say it was this kind of ’losing oneself!’"
"The situation has gradually changed—we’ve been drifting at sea for so long after leaving the lighthouse, it’s certain that the city’s situation has deteriorated," Nina followed beside Sherry, and couldn’t help but look up at her friend, now in a terrifying shape, "...That said, do you need to be scared? You look more frightening than that shadow we just saw."
"What’s frightening? I call this handsome, not scary!" Sherry immediately retorted, then raised her body and looked around, feeling somewhat sentimental, "But speaking of which, there’s a silver lining to this situation—I can roam around the city in this look openly. They act as if they haven’t seen me, even if someone ’awake’ does, they’ll just take it as part of the distortion and won’t come screaming at me with a gun... "
"Just be careful, in case there’s another priest with a working style like Miss Fenna’s patrolling the city and sees you, a Profound Demon, decides to come straight at you with a sword..."
"Then you just splatter his face with sunlight," Sherry casually lifted a skeletal limb and tapped Nina on the shoulder, "Show them why, even at the world’s end, there are still two bright and beautiful girls like us in the city..."
Nina didn’t really want to entertain her friend whose thought process was out of the ordinary.
A "ding-a-ling" of a bell came from the mist, interrupting the girls’ chat, and they both looked up towards the source of the sound to see a steam bus with a bright yellow shell appearing at the street corner. Beneath its heavy body, a dozen pairs of hands and feet grew—the steam bus crawled along the misty street using its limbs, with puffs of white fog spurting from the rear. It stopped at a nearby station, the middle of the cabin tore open, revealing numerous sharp teeth.
"Need a ride? Need a ride? Heading to the museum!" the steam bus loudly called to Sherry and Nina, "Reopened during the curfew, dazzling paintings and textile exhibitions!"
Nina stared dumbfounded at the scene, while Sherry, after being taken aback for a moment, vigorously waved her hands at the swaying bus: "No thanks! I have too many legs to get on the bus!"
"Alright, alright, goodbye, goodbye, I’m off to the next stop!"
The steam bus with the bright yellow shell cheerfully called out, the "door" with countless sharp teeth in the middle of the cabin closed again, and with a puff of steam, it lifted the dozen pairs of limbs underneath and quickly crawled away, disappearing down the road.
Sherry and Nina looked at each other.
The figure of a dog then emerged from the shadow between them, speaking in a muffled voice: "... The Mysterious Deep Sea might be more normal than this place right now."
