Without saying anything further, Nina started walking again towards the direction of home as she remembered it.
Alice and Sherry ignored all those eerie shadows and sounds along the way, and after a while, the familiar little antique shop in the Lower City District finally came into view of the two girls.
Amid the buildings covered with various mysterious shadows and accumulations, even almost transformed into some kind of "living creatures," the small antique shop still retained its long-ago appearance, like a reassuring safe house with warm and bright light shining through its glass display window.
Nina quickly approached and pushed open the un-locked door—the ringing of the bell at the entrance sounded crisply, everything was just like what she remembered.
"Uncle Duncan! Sherry and I are home!" she shouted into the tranquil interior of the antique shop.
But there was no response from within the shop.
"Uncle Duncan, we are home!" Nina called out again.
This time, she finally heard a response—but for a moment, she couldn’t tell if the voice came from her own heart or somewhere inside the shop: "I am behind the counter."
Nina paused for a moment, subconsciously raising her head to look at the counter next to the stairs.
She saw a gaunt and hunched figure, as if merged with the surrounding shadows, sitting silently behind the old speckled wooden counter.
Sherry, having regained her human form, entered the shop with Nina. They passed shelves that seemed not to have been dusted for many days and came to the front of the counter.
"Uncle Duncan..." Nina cautiously stepped forward. She saw that "Uncle Duncan" behind the counter moved his eyeballs slightly, but otherwise, he made no other move, which made her worried, "Are you okay?"
"I have severed most of the connections with this avatar," Duncan’s voice echoed in Nina’s heart, "But I’ve temporarily retained the last bit of vision, sitting here to see you and Sherry safely home—nothing untoward happened on the way, did it?"
Nina stood there somewhat stunned, her eyes revealing complex emotions, but gradually, a warm smile reappeared on her face.
"No," she replied with a smile, standing directly in front of the counter so that "Uncle Duncan," still at the end of the world, could see her more clearly, "Many changes have occurred in the City-State, but nothing dangerous—Mr. Morris has also arrived home safely, and everyone else is fine. Sherry and I just walked here from the commercial street; many people there have already gone to seek refuge."
"That’s good to hear, my range of vision is very limited now, and I have always been curious about the situation outside the door."
"How are things on your side?" Sherry leaned in from beside her, unable to help herself from asking, "Did you and Alice find what you were looking for?"
"We have found it, and now we are preparing to set off and leave this place, heading for our last stop."
"The last stop?" Nina and Sherry exclaimed in unison.
"Yes," Duncan spoke slowly, "Soon, you will be able to see Homeloss again—it will then become the most conspicuous streak of light in the sky."
The uniform grey-white backdrop closed outside the hull, and Homeloss experienced a slight tremble, followed by the return to calmness—in what seemed to be the utmost "stillness," the ship embarked on its final voyage.
Duncan stood at the piloting console at the stern of the ship, with Alice standing beside him, gripping the wheel tightly, controlling the direction of the leap.
"We will first return to the border, but we will not enter the Endless Sea—Homeloss will ’ascend’ at the Eternal Veil, we will cross over the entire world from a very high altitude, straight to the Creation of the World..."
Duncan raised his head, looking into the distance, as if through the grey-white leap conduit, observing the end of time and all things.
"And then, that ’blink of an eye’ moment will arrive."
"Ascend? The Creation of the World?!" Nina’s astonished voice echoed in his heart, "Is that... possible?"
Following that, Sherry’s exclamation also came through: "Homeloss can fly too?"
Duncan began to smile, his lips curving into an arc.
"Yes—it can. After all, the sea of clouds is also a sea."

chapters.title: Chapter 849 - 846: The Sunlit Voyage
chapters.content:
Chapter 849: Chapter 846: The Sunlit Voyage
Fenna stood atop the tallest tower of the Storm Cathedral, gazing out through the open window. Her eyes swept over the cathedral’s rooftops, the twinkling lights deep within the mist, the city districts whose buildings no longer matched her memory, and the direction of the distant sea.
Beside the tower’s spiral staircase, the steam-powered pipes emitted a faint hiss. Copper incense burners hung from the pipes’ valves, wafting threads of smoke. The aged Archbishop Valentin stood silently nearby, his murky pale eyes, clouded from blood no longer flowing, looking into the distance with Fenna.
It was only after an indeterminate time that Fenna softly broke the silence: "I remember... I often stood on this tower too, whenever night fell, I watched over every corner of Prand, with the hissing of the steam pipes always present, and the scent of the incense bringing tranquility."
"It seems like that was only recently," murmured Archbishop Valentin.
"Yes, it feels like it was just recently," Fenna nodded slightly, "those nights were always restless, with all sorts of things emerging from the darkness, disturbing the lives of ordinary people. Back then, I was full of confidence, feeling capable of confronting any threat to the City-State—be it the shadows of the Heretics, or the creatures summoned by them."
The elderly Archbishop said nothing more, merely lowering his gaze toward the direction of the cathedral’s garden. Through the foggy night, faint roars and spine-chilling crunching sounds seemed to suggest a colossal creature trapped deep within the mist.
"Trennie is dining again," Valentin spoke slowly, "at this time each day, she devours herself, and twenty-four hours later, she is reborn from the soil. There are also twelve Nuns and twelve Fathers wandering near Trennie, entering the small arcade next to the garden at specific times—the very place you used to walk by every day."
Fenna let out an imperceptible sigh, speaking softly: "Do they ever run outside the cathedral?"
"I have ordered the garden to be sealed off, but it wouldn’t make a difference even if it wasn’t," said Valentin, "Trennie never leaves the garden, not even when ’alive,’ and as for those nuns and fathers, they are not dangerous—the city is filled with shadows far more dangerous than them."
"My sword finds no use here," Fenna lamented.
"Should wanderers attempt to breach the high walls of the Shelters, we would still need your strength," Valentin shook his head, "there’s chaos of all magnitudes constantly arising in the city. Sometimes, it’s people suddenly ’awakening’ in their homes, sometimes it’s blind wanderers breaking through the security zones. We’ve arranged for a new ’Vigilant Guard’ to patrol and guard various parts of the city, but there are moments when they can’t cover everything. If you’re willing, I think they would be very welcoming of you, ’Judge,’ to return and continue leading them."
The old Archbishop paused for a moment before adding, "Of course, you might need to readjust to your old subordinates, some of the Vigilant Guard have gone through a...’transformation’ that makes them look less human. But in this world today, to possess reason and humanity is already an extremely precious thing."
"I won’t mind," Fenna smiled, slightly moving her arm, "after all, it’s still better than the ’human content’ on the Homeloss, right? I am very willing to return to this familiar work—you can arrange it for me."
"That’s good," Valentin smiled as well, the elderly man nodding, "I’ll gather the Vigilant Guard during the next shift change to convey this good news. Would you like to rest in your room until then? It’s still in good condition, and someone has been cleaning it."
"Alright," Fenna said casually, but then as if she remembered something, she asked with some concern, "Is there anything to be mindful of?"
"Don’t mind the murmurs of the vanity on your dressing table—it’s not a voice with reason. And don’t look out the window for too long; it tends to grow eyes. That’s about it."
"...Honestly, it’s quite... ’mild,’" said Fenna.
Valentin shrugged helplessly, but just then, a mysterious light suddenly emerged from somewhere, interrupting what he was about to say.
Both lifted their heads in astonishment, searching for the source of the light.
The clouds were tinged with a cold and pale light—the glow that fell from the Creation of the World. As the cloud layer lowered, that scar spanning the entire sky was now entirely on the backside of the clouds, rendering it difficult to make out from the ground. Only within the brightest crevices of the clouds and the thinnest parts could one occasionally glimpse a fraction of the crack’s structure.
And now, between the gaps in the clouds, they saw an unusual glimmer of light.
It wasn’t the cold, pale glow, but instead a faint orange hue. It mingled with the original light from the Creation of the World, and for a moment, it evoked the long-lost image of... sunlight.
Fenna was somewhat astonished; she looked up toward the Creation of the World, and through a slit in the churning cloud layer she finally saw the massive "scar," where the strange orange glow—reminiscent of sunlight—was surprisingly radiating from the edge of the Creation of the World.
It looked as if an intense light source was erupting from behind the Creation of the World, obscured by fissures in the sky, with only a faint scattering of residual light slipping out from the edges, dimly permeating the sky.
Valentin also immediately made the same association. With an expression of utter bewilderment, the old Archbishop looked at the sky: "What is that..."
Fenna did not respond to the old man, and in the next moment, the orange glow diffusing from behind the Creation of the World gradually dimmed and went out completely.
A moment later, the orange light reappeared and spread across the sky.
The invisible yet powerful light source flickered, like a guiding lamp in the night sky.
The entire world could see this spectacle.
Even all dimensions could witness this scene.
At the world’s end, in the "frontier node" where the gods slumber, the dim and false sunlight once dispersed the mist, illuminating the Leviathan Queen’s palace, the server matrix of Navigation #2, the Ashen Isle of the King of Fire, and the graveyard of death.
In the deepest depths of the Mysterious Deep Sea, Navigation #1, which has lost control and is proliferating, is slowly crawling along the mysterious depths. A colossal swarm of nanomachines almost fill every inch of space beneath those shattered lands, among countless wild tendrils, the dim sunlight suddenly scatters the darkness, shining upon the dark red core of Navigation #1.
In the remote northern ice fields of the Endless Sea, ice sculptures stand silently beside the massive archives buildings. The Torchbearers are frozen in the ice fields, with the tallest among them still maintaining a posture of looking southward before being frozen—
The distant and dim "sunlight" twinkles, and even after being obstructed and weakened by the Creation of the World, it still casts a radiant glow on those icy faces, as if to deeply imprint in every pair of frozen eyes.
This sunlight is toxic, for all mortal beings in the Endless Sea, bathing in such sunlight is no different from immersing in the whispers of Subspace.
But with the obstruction and weakening by the Creation of the World, its impact on the mortal realm has been minimized—even if there is still some "poison," that influence can be disregarded.
Besides, this world itself is already deeply immersed in distortion and twist—faced with the collapse of everything, the radiance of the Black Sun is not much more severe than the world’s own fall.
And so, for the first time, the exiled sun began to shine uninhibitedly—after such a prolonged exile, after all those Scions of the Sun who once longed for Its light but never received, had been dissipated into history, It finally blazes boldly in the apocalypse.
Sunlight spreads through the transition channel, outlining a bright and clear "path of light" against that extreme uniform gray-white backdrop.
Duncan felt a slight shake under his feet. Alice was fine-tuning the transition process, beginning to correct their course along the navigation signal released by the Black Sun.
Duncan narrowed his eyes slightly, gazing toward the light at the end of the channel—here, without the shielding of the Creation of the World, that sunlight spanned time and space and even seemed a bit dazzling.
"I will light a beacon for you among the night sky, that you shall sail toward the brightest direction..."
A civilization that created a Dyson sphere, they may not have developed to the technological height of the New Hope, but they clearly have learned how to send their own signals in the universe, at least able to produce a signal sufficient to navigate starships.
"I see the light, we are sailing in your direction, this should shorten the journey of Homeloss through transition," Duncan said to the sunlight, knowing that the Black Sun could hear his voice in this way, "How are you doing now?"
"The scorching burning process, I feel like I’m boiling in the flames—it hurts, but this is good," the voice of the Black Sun trembled in the sunlight, "This is the first time I truly burn in ten thousand years. I thought I couldn’t bear all this, but... it’s good."
"In the new world, you can coexist harmoniously with your own sunlight, free from the pain of being scorched by yourself," Duncan said with a hint of a smile on his face, "There will be a rule that allows for such a thing."
"...Is that possible?"
"Yes, it’s a one-time opportunity to customize the new world," Duncan said slowly, "You can even ask for some value-added services—like turning your sunlight pink."
"Ah ha, no need for that, but if possible, I do have an additional idea..."
"Oh?"
"Can you arrange for me a few more planets? Gaseous or rocky ones are fine... Observing the evolution of life on different planets might be a very entertaining thing."
"Alright, I’ve noted that—this wish will come after Alice’s frying pan."
"That’s quite an honor."

chapters.title: Chapter 850 - 847: Depth 3, Nightfall
chapters.content:
Chapter 850: Chapter 847: Depth 3, Nightfall
In each upcoming day, everyone on the Endless Sea witnessed the shimmer of the Black Sun—a false sunlight that permeated and enveloped the world. Behind the Creation of the World, the last lighthouse on this sea transmitted its brilliance to every corner of the Shelter, continuously for many days and nights.
People speculated about the origins of this "brilliance." Some speculated it was a sign of the world’s further collapse, others guessed that it was some change occurring in the Creation of the World. The ultimate optimists believed it was the sunlight that would soon descend upon the earth again, while the ultimate pessimists believed it was time for all things to meet their end—but for many others... they paid no attention to this sunlight.
Having lost their self-awareness, entities wandered blindly through the streets in the fog and night, gnawing and tearing at what they "recognized" as food. Their deep roars seemed to fill the entire world, while layers of murmuring whispers emerged from deep beneath the City-State;
Giant, fluctuating shadows appeared on the sea, gathering towards the City-State’s coastline. These were fleets from various corners of history, returning home, unidentified sailors, and pirates made visible and forgotten in the night, boarding the City-State only to merge back into the night amid howls, their whereabouts unknown. But whispers of low, blurred sea songs and calls seemed to emanate from every dock and intersection;
City buildings awoke in the night. After the last lucid person had left them, they forgot their original forms in the fog. Roofs opened their staggered, scattered eyes, chimneys grew and coiled in the night, windows sprouted sharp teeth, and every door sang loudly in the dark, creating the most tumultuous noise remembered by the City-State;
And those who awakened, the true madmen, built high walls deep within the city.
They maintained contact with each other through sewers and the few still-operating urban transit systems, with survivors from city halls and churches ensuring the last semblance of order.
People took turns sleeping, ensuring that in these last Shelters, there was at least one pair of eyes open in every corner, to prevent those walls and roofs from growing scales and flesh.
The watchmen moved through the night, searching for the last survivors in city areas that had completely twisted and fallen, to prevent them from being devoured and erased by other dehumanized entities.
Everyone received the final order—an order that first originated from a distant northern City-State, and was then transmitted throughout the world with the establishment and communication of various City-State unions. Its core message was simple:
Survive, by all possible means, and do not let too many fall before the last darkness before dawn.
Even though the death mechanisms had stopped, those devoured by the night and madness still disappeared from this world. They turned into useless remnants in the Shelters, unable to witness the "dawn"—the world’s last protectors must prevent this at all costs.
And those protected, inside high walls, cautiously yet hopefully and expectantly talked about that "dawn."
Everyone spoke of a new world that would arise at the end of this long night.
No one knew how the news first spread nor if it was an intentional guide by the protectors. It might just be a distant and elusive hope, but amidst this night of sinking everything, hope had to spread and flourish.
Lawrence stood quietly on a piece of old city wall in the western district of Phaeron, gazing into the distance.
This section of the old wall had recently been repaired and fortified; now it was part of the Shelter in this border City-State. The protective high wall extended from the port area and met near the steam hub’s factory building, enclosing nearly all the survivors in the city.
The remaining few survivors were gathered outside the high walls in two churches and nearby apartment buildings. The watchmen were trying to connect some of the Shelter’s underground structures to bring everyone under protection.
There were terrifying roars from the depths of the night, mixed with the sounds of a steam-walking machine firing. A series of flashes appeared deep in the shifting fog, and then everything gradually returned to tranquility—after a long while, a flare rose in that direction, bursting into a persistent glow in the night sky.
The faint "sunlight" escaping from behind the Creation of the World was reflected in the light of the flare.
"It seems that there are no more survivors in that direction, only monsters bred by the city itself," Martha’s voice came from the little mirror on Lawrence’s chest, "It’s about time, there probably won’t be any more ’awakeners’ appearing in those long-occupied districts."
"Phaeron is a small city, the search will end soon, and in the days to come, the main task of the watchman forces will be to ensure the safety inside the high walls," Lawrence nodded slightly, "But in other City-States, the search for survivors would probably continue until the end... In those vast maze-like old districts, there are always people still holding on, waiting for rescue..."
Martha hummed softly and did not speak again.
The "sunlight" behind the Creation of the World slowly dimmed and then reemerged, lighting up the entire sky.
"...Who would have thought that the ’Black Sun’ would be the last thing to light up the sky," Martha broke the silence softly, "Even a year ago, such madness wouldn’t even be spoken by the Believers of the sun."
"But now, besides us, no one in this world remembers what the ’Black Sun’ is," Lawrence sighed and shook his head, "All the fear and worship concerning It had been folded into abandoned history."
He lifted his head, looking at the dim yellow sunlight spreading across the sky.
The "Black Sun," long forgotten by the entire world, still faintly flickered behind the Creation of the World, while no creature on this world needed Its light anymore.
It merely lit the navigational beacon for the last ship still voyaging in this world.
Footsteps came from behind. Lawrence withdrew his gaze from the sky, turned around, and saw a gaunt, ugly figure wearing an ill-fitting crew uniform approaching through the fog, stepping onto the city wall to face him.
"Captain, I’ve returned to report." The sailor tugged at the hem of his crew uniform, his mouth twisting into a grotesque and startling smile.
Lawrence sized up the sailor with a twinge in the corner of his eye: "Can you not smile like that every time you see me? It’s quite frightening."
The sailor immediately grinned wider: "On my way here, I observed the area beyond the high walls. With this appearance, I’m already above average in today’s City-State."
Lawrence spat to the side but refrained from teasing the cadaver any further. Instead, he stepped forward and patted the sailor on the shoulder.
"How is it on Homeloss?"
After pondering for a moment, the deep furrows on the sailor’s face slowly smoothed out: "It’s a nice place."
"That’s good," Lawrence smiled, then shook his head with a smile, "So now the pleasant external assignment is over..."
He opened his arms, making a welcoming gesture: "Welcome back to the White Oak."
The sailor smiled too, and reached out his arms: "It’s an honor."
Lawrence dodged to the side: "I’m just showing appreciation, an actual hug—forget it—go take a good bath first, your rotten flesh is already souring."
...
"Professor Morris has already taken his family to the Shelter. Now he has signed up for the city wall guard squad... It’s said that at first, the head of the guards refused him because he was old, but then the Professor ended up beating everyone present..."
"Miss Fenna is now staying at the cathedral—she commands the Night Watch troops there. It is said that there are many uncontrolled priests confined in the cathedral. She’s busy every day, but I felt she was quite happy last time I saw her... She also told you? Yes, she’s very happy she can help back in City-State..."
"Both the sailor and Miss Agatha have reached their destinations safely, right? That’s great... I’ve heard that ships heading north are getting fewer, and they say the situation in the Chill Sea isn’t good. There were some concerns before... Safe arrival is good, that was probably the last fleet."
"How is Miss Lukrecia doing? Trying the cuisine in Light Breeze Harbor? Really?... That’s so like the witch lady..."
Nina’s muttering voice echoed in my heart. Duncan sat on the large wooden barrel at the edge of Homeloss’s deck, listening to the distant voices, a faint smile on his face.
"Do you and Sherry have any plans?" he suddenly asked.
There was silence from Nina for a few seconds: "... Sherry and I decided to just stay in the antique shop."
"Aren’t you going to the Shelter or the cathedral? It might be a bit better over there."
"No, we don’t have other relatives, and we aren’t worried about safety either, staying in the Shelter isn’t much meaningful—now Sherry and the dog patrol the shop, I maintain the light and temperature in the antique shop. This little shop is also a kind of ’Shelter’ for this street block. Occasionally, when Night Watch troops pass by, they can come in and rest. They are all Fenna’s subordinates... Oh yes, they also say this antique shop is ’the most reliable nocturnal haven in the City-State’..."
Nina’s voice sounded cheerful with a hint of pride, she seemed quite satisfied with the current situation, and Duncan, listening, put aside his little worry.
It looks like those two girls have managed the small antique shop in their own way, and managed it quite vibrantly.
While Nina chattered about everyday matters, Duncan’s peripheral vision caught the silhouettes of light emerging at the end of the transit channel.
The outlines of clouds appeared in the depths of the grey-white background, the "sunlight" pervasive in the entire transit channel casting over those distant clouds, sketching the silhouette of the Eternal Veil.
Duncan slowly stood up.
"Nina."
The girl, chattering about everyday affairs, immediately stopped: "Hmm?"
"Get ready to look up—"

chapters.title: Chapter 851 - 848: Depth 2, Annihilation
chapters.content:
Chapter 851: Chapter 848: Depth 2, Annihilation
Now, the jump drive has reached its endpoint — Homeloss has once again returned to the confines of the sea and fog after the lengthy voyage beyond the borders came to an end.
But this is just a temporary respite within the entire journey; Duncan’s goal was not to return to the Endless Sea, but rather to head towards that suspended, frozen doomsday in the sky.
With minor vibrations emanating from various parts of the ship, Homeloss disengaged from jump state, the phantom of New Hope rapidly dissipating in the sky, and those countless invisible threads retract back into the doll’s body. The distinctive thick fog of the border seas almost instantly surged from all directions, enveloping the entire ship like fervent greeters—Homeloss steered through the dense fog, gliding across the calm, mirror-like sea, with the ship gradually steadying itself.
Alice blinked, her eyes quickly regaining alertness. She looked up to see Duncan standing by her side and her face broke into a smile: "Captain! We’re back!"
"Yes, back to the Endless Sea. From here on, I’ll take the helm," Duncan said with a smile, nodding at the doll as he stepped up to the dark, heavy steering wheel, "Go take a rest, or you can just watch from the side."
"Mhm, I’m not tired, I’ll watch from the side!" Alice cheerfully said, grabbing a large wooden bucket to sit by the corner of the driver’s stand, propping her chin in her hands as she watched Duncan take the wheel.
Duncan turned to give the doll lady a helpless smile before gripping the heavy steering wheel with both hands.
The ethereal green Spiritual Fire burned between his fingers, spreading in all directions along the steering wheel, igniting the deck and the masts; the translucent sails of Spiritual Body billowed and swelled in the intangible wind—Homeloss burned brightly, just as on the day in Duncan’s memory when he first took hold of the helm.
Afterward, Duncan closed his eyes—not to focus on the Endless Sea, nor on the Eternal Veil. In his gradually shutting perception, all he could see was a slowly flickering, cold, and false sunlight sketching out a bright pathway in the darkness, pointing far into the distance.
He heard a deep roar emanating from deep within Homeloss, heard the rigging tremble in the air, and the creaking in the cabins; these overlapping sounds were like incessant cheers, and amid the ship’s cheering, he heard the strange, off-key voice of the goat-headed figure begin to resonate.
It was a peculiar song, one he had never heard before, and he couldn’t understand the lyrics with their intricate tunes and strange articulations, which seemed to traverse vast periods of time, a hymn from some ancient era meant to please deities, not at all pleasant to the ear.
But Duncan, with his eyes closed, seemed to "see" something amidst that bizarre off-key hum.
He saw brilliant sunlight, majestic mountains, and rivers; he saw a colossal tree taking root on the earth, and the creator strolling slowly from the valley amidst the Dreamscape.
The creatures with newly awakened minds gathered around the great tree, using colorful stones and furs to decorate the resting place for the creator, excitedly playing their crude, primitive instruments, chanting in the dawn and dusk those hymns praising the gentle breeze and sunlight.
Now, after such a long passage of time, their creator has remembered this melody.
Then, Homeloss began to accelerate slowly again—the off-tune hum of the goat’s head turned into the final sailor’s song on the voyage, as the enormous Ghost Ship further shed its corporeal form amid the burning of the Spiritual Fire, revealing an even more thorough ethereal texture than before.
The flames rose higher and higher until they consumed the ship, consumed all its history, every foundation that had ever existed, all the projections it had cast across dimensions, and every data unit it had occupied as an "entity" in this tiny Shelter—the pale purple starlight suffused within the flames, and Homeloss finally transformed into a vast, almost indistinguishable phantom in the fire.
This phantom had no weight; it drifted upwards amidst the clouds that enveloped the whole world, following the course delineated by the distant, illusory sunlight, and gradually accelerating towards the sky.
Zhou Ming gripped the helm tightly; for the first time, he felt this world so tangibly—felt his presence here, felt the existence of Homeloss, and felt... that he was a part of this broken, dim, and gradually cooling world.
He was one of the countless Displaced of this world.
Zhou Ming still kept his eyes tightly shut, to avoid the excessive "observation" that could cause the Endless Sea to collapse in an instant, but his "perception"—had already commenced the final destruction process of this world.
Starlight began to rise from the edges of the Shelter; now, all the underlying data of this Shelter had opened its doors to him, the final disaster backup began to be imported into the database of the Reverse Singularity—with this ultimate "import" process underway, the "reset" operation starting from the external barrier was also initiated.
Nina and Sherry stared with wide eyes in astonishment.
They made their way to the second floor of the antique shop, also bringing along Uncle Duncan’s body to the window beside the second floor—even though the body had completely ceased to function, Nina still placed it beside her, to "watch" the outside situation together.
The two girls looked up at the southeastern sky.
A dazzling brilliance was rising from that direction, on a trajectory that was slow yet breathtaking, moving towards the Creation of the World.
That dazzling light, mixed with pale green and purple hues, even brightened half of the sky, bringing a dawn-like "daylight" to the end of this stretched-out night for the world.
"Wow..."
Sherry craned her neck with effort, stretching it out long, and let out an exaggerated exclamation; then she vigorously tugged on the chain around A-Dog’s neck, clamoring excitedly: "A-Dog, A-Dog, look at that! Over there at the sky’s edge! The Captain’s really flying up! He’s heading towards the Creation of the World! It’s starting, it’s starting!"
"I see it, I see it, don’t fling the chain," A-Dog shouted, pressing down on the chain with his paw, "Quick, find a stable place to lean against, the final moment is starting, you’ve been going on about when it will start every single day, well now..."
"I... I’m a bit nervous..." Sherry suddenly became anxious, she clung to A-Dog’s chain and leaned against the wall, but soon she moved back to the window, "What will happen? Will it hurt? Or will it just swish—pass in an instant? Will there be a bright light?"
"How would I know, I..." A’Gou muttered but suddenly stopped again.
The flames imbued with starlight were burning in every crevice of its bones, in a completely uncontrolled state, bursting and rising from within it.
Sherry blinked and raised her arm to see the same flames igniting on her body, and through the flickering light of the flames, she saw Nina also gradually being enveloped by the fire.
"Uncle Duncan is observing this world through our eyes..." Nina quickly realized, unruffled, she softly spoke with a gentle expression, "Don’t be afraid."
"I...I’m not afraid, but what should I do?" Sherry asked with a voice clearly tinged with fear as she looked towards Nina, "Just look around with wide eyes, right?"
"Observing the world through our eyes is just a metaphor, actually..." Nina began to explain subconsciously, but halfway through, she caught sight of her friend’s pure and unsophisticated expression and swallowed the rest of her explanation, ending with a somewhat helpless smile, "Alright, just look around with wide eyes, after all, Uncle Duncan will arrange everything..."
"Oh... Oh!" Sherry hastily agreed, and truly widened her eyes as she tried her best to look into the distance.
And in the corner of Nina’s eye, at the very end of the clouds covering the whole world, a magnificent view never seen before in the real dimension was slowly ascending into the sky, like a curtain merging towards heaven—
The stars were rising.
The Endless Sea began to collapse silently from the outside in, amidst the stardust.
First to go were the border outposts, lighthouses, and mobile ports established by the Tetragod Church in the remote sea regions, as well as the patrol fleets that always stayed close to the Eternal Veil.
Next were the frontier islands where explorers had once stopped, leaving behind countless stories.
Following that, came the City-States located in the border seas...
Lucresia stood on the highest deck of the Brilliant Starship, currently docked at the Light Breeze Harbor—she was grabbing Rabi’s arm with one hand and supporting with the other hand the tiny doll Niru, who was sitting on her shoulder just a few dozen centimeters tall.
The clockwork doll Luny stood unwavering behind Lucresia, as always.
Together, they silently watched the multitude of stars rise from the borders of the world, approaching and rolling in like a grand curtain reaching from earth to heaven.
The stars first touched a platform on the distant sea—a facility once used to study the "Luminous Geometric Body," now deserted with the City-State unable to reclaim it, left as a solitary monument upon the sea.
Without any process of disintegration, without sound, and without any flash—the platform silently merged with the stars, leaving no trace, and beyond the light of the stars was nothing but utter void.
Niru hugged Lucresia’s head tightly, her small body trembling, "Mistress, I’m a bit scared..."
"Don’t worry, Niru," Lucresia raised her hand, gently patting the little doll’s back, "The next time you open your eyes, we will be at our new home."
"...Okay." The little doll nodded vigorously.
"Mistress..."
Luny’s voice came from behind; Lucresia turned her head and saw the clockwork doll looking slightly anxious.
"Are you also scared?"
"...A little."
Lucresia smiled, "Then close your eyes, and when you open them again, it’ll be like... just a blink."
Luny hesitated for a moment, then obediently closed her eyes.
In the last glimpse of peripheral vision, she saw her mistress’s figure silently disappearing into the starlight.

chapters.title: Chapter 852 - 849: Depth 1, Return to Silence
chapters.content:
Chapter 852: Chapter 849: Depth 1, Return to Silence
The observational signal from Lucrecia disappeared, and correspondingly, all the data and materials about Light Breeze Harbor were imported in the instant before the reset.
Zhou Ming calmly perceived the changes occurring in this Shelter—sensing the gradual collapse and dissolution of the frontier, sensing the Endless Sea breaking apart bit by bit, sensing city-states vanishing into nothingness among the stars. He heard many voices, as well as countless confused, fearful, desperate, and hopeful thoughts. Tens of thousands of minds spoke to him at the same moment, then fell silent at the same moment, and then this process repeated over and over...
Yet his own mind seemed to have transcended this process—the Reverse Singularity was slowly awakening. He had almost all his attention focused on maintaining the stability and controllability of this process until, after an unknown amount of time, he finally had the spare energy to pay attention to the situation around him.
His eyes were closed, but he "saw" Alice. The doll lady was still sitting not far away, watching intently over here, seemingly unconcerned about everything happening outside Homeloss.
He also "saw" Homeloss. He saw the ship floating on a sea of clouds, like a blazing, pure illusion. Most of the ship had vanished in that fierce burning, with only the core structures remaining under his feet at the helm, and part of the stern deck—beyond these structures was a "light fog" trailing magnificent tails, like stellar ejecta.
The humming of the goat’s head continued intermittently, that astonishing spine of the ancient gods floated deep in the light fog, still undergoing its final burning.
Zhou Ming heard footsteps.
The "Door of the Displaced" standing on the stern deck suddenly opened, and Lei Nora walked out from it. The Frost Queen stood quietly gazing at the sea of clouds in the distance, watching the world gradually disappear in the starlight. After a while, she turned and walked towards the direction of the helm—she climbed the stairs suffused with starlight and came to Zhou Ming, who was steering the ship.
"I thought you had already left," Zhou Ming said with a slight smile on his face. "The bindings of Homeloss are gone. Your ’Drifting Home’ should be able to leave this place at any time."
"True, I could leave, but where to go at this time—when the whole world is gradually disappearing? After leaving, it would probably soon be swallowed by that starlight," Lei Nora said with a smile, then shook her head. "I thought about it and decided to stay here. This is the best seat to watch the end of the world, an event like this... you won’t encounter again if you miss it."
Zhou Ming said nothing more, just nodded slightly, continuing to grip the helm tightly, sailing together with the ship toward that distant sunlight in the darkness.
The sunlight dimmed slowly, then brightened again. Amidst the wantonly spreading brilliance, he felt as if he could already see that magnificent corona, and the ancient "deity" beneath the corona.
In his mind, voices from afar occasionally reached him—these were his "Observation Nodes" left above the disintegrating, vanishing Endless Sea.
"...This is Frost. The starlight is gradually spreading from the direction of the Permafrost Sea Area," Tyrion told him. "The distant ocean surface has disappeared, and a clear rift has appeared in the clouds... It’s spectacular. We’ve made our preparations here."
Then came Agatha’s voice: "Many survivors have gathered in the cathedral. I am with the other ’Agatha’. We are accompanying the children here... They don’t know what happened. I’ve told the children that this is a necessary process to welcome the ’dawn,’ and that everything will soon be alright."
"Phaeron has also observed the starlight appearing above the western sea region, and it’s rapidly approaching us. There’s some unrest in the city now, but it’s not too bad—after all, it’s just a moment," the sailor’s voice sounded carefree. "I’m with Captain Lawrence, we are standing on the city walls, along with the others from the White Oak. We’ve just agreed that when the starlight arrives, we’ll close our eyes together, count to three, and then open them..."
"This is Prand, nothing has happened here yet, only the stars at the edge of the sky are visible," Maurice’s voice spoke. "I’m with my family, and we can see the trail you left in the sky... It’s magnificent, and impressive."
Zhou Ming silently listened to these voices coming from afar, while perceiving the various changes occurring in the Shelter through the beacons left in the Endless Sea, then after a long time, he nodded gently: "Thank you for your perseverance."
A response came through the mental connection from each person—and then, the signals from Tyrion and Agatha vanished.
Followed by the sailor, Lawrence, and others.
Several hours later, more than half of the city-states over the Endless Sea had dissolved into the rising, closing curtain of stars. This Shelter, built by ancient kings and running for ten thousand years after the end of the world, was now gradually shrinking to only a third of its size.
And it continued to shrink rapidly.
In Prand, the last light illuminated the night sky of the City-State, chaotic roars of those blind entities of chaos came from deep within the clouds, massive invisible shadows writhed and grew between the rooftops and towers of the city, as if a final revelry, reaching out to the converging starlight curtain in the distance.
Fenna and Heidi stood together on the high walls of the Upper City District Shelter, and when the circular curtain of starlight rose from all around, Heidi couldn’t help but exclaim softly, "It’s so beautiful..."
Fenna turned with a smile: "Didn’t I tell you, the captain always makes a grand spectacle of things—you didn’t believe me."
Heidi spread her hands helplessly: "My ’knight lady’, don’t forget that I’ve always stayed inside the City-State, I haven’t seen as much of the world as you have out there."
"...Isn’t the mental world of a psychiatric patient enough for you to see the world?"
"...The end of the world is upon us, can we stop talking about work," Heidi immediately tugged at the corners of her mouth, "Having said that, I really hope that ’New World’s’ psychiatrists won’t need to combat delusions in patients’ minds with a gun anymore..."
The two longtime friends began discussing matters of the New World atop the high walls, while Maurice stood behind them at a short distance, his expression complex. It took him a while before he lowered his voice and muttered to his wife beside him, "Do you think... our daughter and Fenna are a bit too close..."
"...Impossible, right?"
"I used to think it was impossible too, but the captain once said, it’s possible..."
Several hours later, the curtain of starlight finally spread across the sea near Pland.
Sherry instinctively grasped Nina’s hand, looking nervously at the stars that almost covered the entire sky. Under the glorious starlight, the incessant roars and bizarre whispers of the city seemed to rapidly fade away, and the whole world was becoming... exceptionally quiet.
The voice of A Dog came from the shadows at her feet: "Pland is situated at the center of the Endless Sea... Starlight converges outside the coastline of the City-State, and now only this city remains in the world."
"I used to dislike this city," Sherry couldn’t help but mutter softly, "those alleys always flooded and stinking to high heaven, the houses that never warmed up, and the rumbling factories, but now... I’m somewhat reluctant to leave them."
Nina did not speak; she just gently patted Sherry’s hand and then bent down to straighten ’Uncle Duncan’s’ collar, pushing him towards the window once more.
She knew Uncle Duncan could no longer observe this world with his own eyes, but she was aware that he still had the final, faintest connection with this incarnation; by doing so, she might give comfort to Uncle Duncan as he sailed towards doom.
"Uncle Duncan, the lights on the city’s edge have disappeared. I saw the tallest rooftop in Cross District merging into the starlight just now; it looks like it’s our turn soon."
Nina looked up at the magnificent trail of fire slowly sweeping across the sky from behind the clouds—the part of that blaze had now entered the back of the Creation of the World, only the gorgeous tail flame was still casting heart-stirring radiance, reflected in her eyes.
Soon, she heard the response from the bottom of her heart: "Yes, I’m almost there."
"Hmm... Is it dark where you are?"
"In the absence of sunlight, it is very dark. The back of the Creation of the World is pitch black and does not emit the pale light seen from the side of the Endless Sea. But when the sunlight emerges, it will be very bright—the Black Sun is just ahead, I can see it now."
"Hmm, then take care on your way, Sherry and I will be waiting for you."
"Okay."
The voice in her mind faded, and Nina squinted her eyes slightly, watching the magnificent flame in the sky being gradually obscured by the Creation of the World, while in the periphery of her vision, another neighborhood silently dissolved into the stellar expanse.
Starlight was converging above Pland; only the last few buildings remained in this world.
Sherry’s hand reached out again; this seemingly carefree person was surprisingly timid.
Nina smiled and grasped Sherry’s hand, slowly narrowing her eyes at the pervasive starlight in the sky, murmuring as if talking to herself—
"You march forward... don’t worry, just keep moving forward..."
She turned her head back, watching Sherry’s eyes amidst the spreading glow of starlight.
"Sherry, it’s okay to blink now."
Then, the starlight finally completely converged above Pland, the last physical area within the Endless Sea being quietly swallowed into the depths of the stars. All sounds of the world, all matter, all history that had ever existed, all that was born, destroyed, great, mediocre, noble, sinful... all dissipated into this silent nothingness.
And so, the world was destroyed.

chapters.title: Chapter 853 - 850: Depth 0, Assignment
chapters.content:
Chapter 853: Chapter 850: Depth 0, Assignment
Now, everything has quieted down.
Whether it was the voices from the mind or the environment sensed through various "nodes", whether it was Nina’s gentle admonishments or Fenna and Morris’s calm reports, all have disappeared from this world along with the closing of the stars—the world itself has also turned into nothingness.
This small shelter, built by the ancient kings, quietly vanished into the stars of the new world after operating for ten thousand years.
Now, in this primitive and chaotic Sea of Information formed by the remnants of many worlds, only the last ship is still sailing on its final voyage.
The Homeloss sails on the backside of the Creation of the World, and right below the "hull" lies the "rift" that had spanned across the sky of the Endless Sea for ten thousand years. People never imagined that the backside of this "rift" presents a completely different scene than its front—
Zhou Ming stands beside the steering wheel of the Homeloss, and now that the world has been destroyed, he no longer needs to worry about his observations destroying the Endless Sea, so he opened his eyes—looking downward through the nearly burned-out deck and hull gaps, he saw the pitch-black rift extending infinitely into the distance, emitting no light, almost as if actively absorbing all light, presenting an extreme deep black that could almost give the sense of "infinite falling," and although the details were not clear in the dark depths, there was a vague sense revealing a feeling of "sinking down," as if... there was a vast space inside.
The Black Sun still hung high above that pitch-black rift, in the vast boundless chaos and darkness, the splendid and magnificent sun still changed its luminance according to its rules, emitting strong and clear navigation signals—even though the Homeloss no longer needed its guidance anymore.
Zhou Ming then turned his head to look at the doll who still remained by his side.
Alice was no longer sitting on the barrel because even that barrel had been burned to ashes by the starlight flames a few minutes ago, and she now stood beside Zhou Ming on the last small piece of the deck—Lei Nora stood by the doll’s side.
"What are you thinking about?" Zhou Ming suddenly asked.
"Thinking about nothing!" Alice immediately replied cheerfully, but then she scratched her head, feeling that might be a bit off, and after briefly thinking it over, she smiled and added, "It feels very interesting—so the backside of the Creation of the World looks like this."
"Aren’t you scared?" Even though he already knew the answer, Zhou Ming still asked curiously.
"Not scared," the doll indeed shook her head, "although I also don’t know why I’m not scared..."
Zhou Ming smiled, then looked up to Lei Nora: "And you?"
"I was thinking... when the world ends, it is so quiet," Lei Nora said calmly, slowly speaking, "From a very young age, I always heard and saw those things transmitted from the deep sea, those distorted and torn scenes and the chaotic roars and low hums brought me immense fear, I always thought, the apocalypse would be like that, in great fear and earth-shattering changes, all things crying out as they were torn into pieces.
"But in reality, the apocalypse is so quiet, everything has disappeared, at the last moment, this world did not make any sound, neither the roars of the brave nor the wails of the cowards... nothing, so quiet that it even feels surreal, making me think that the world still exists, that if I ’go down’ from here, I would still see the endless blue sea and the sunlight scattered on the sea surface."
Zhou Ming didn’t speak, and Lei Nora, after being quiet for a few seconds, gently sighed: "I should leave now."
"Leaving now?" Zhou Ming raised his eyebrows, "There’s nowhere to go now."
"I know, but I now have to let the ’Drifting House’ break away from here," Lei Nora said with a smile, "The scenery of the apocalypse, I have seen it, in the new world, I still hope to continue my journey."
"...I understand," Zhou Ming gently nodded, then showed a slight smile to the "Frost Queen," "Then I wish you a safe journey—Homeloss will always have a door open for your ’Drifting House,’ even in the new world."
"Thank you," Lei Nora smiled and took a step back, "See you in the new world."
She left the only remaining control deck of the ship, went through the fragmented staircase and the few remaining shattered pieces of the deck, and entered the still quietly standing "Door of the Displaced," and shortly after, a streak of light appeared at the edge of the flames of the Homeloss, glittering momentarily in the brilliance of the stars ... and disappeared.
Afterward, the deck of the control station contracted once more, collapsed, and the remaining parts of the Homeloss further disintegrated in the blaze of starlight, followed by a gradually deepening roar as the illusion of the mast completely disappeared, and then the structure connected to the steering wheel.
Zhou Ming raised his head, glanced at the distant "sunlight," then lowered his gaze to the last bit of the steering wheel remains in his hand—after a moment, he let go.
"Well done," he whispered to the ship.
He stepped towards the edge of the control deck, passed through the nearly transparent remnants of light and shadow of the once-existing staircase and deck, with Alice following closely behind him—they arrived in front of the door of the captain’s room at the stern, while the "Captain’s Room" was almost non-existent by then.

chapters.title: Chapter 854 - 850: Depth 0, Assignment_2
chapters.content:
Chapter 854: Chapter 850: Depth 0, Assignment_2
Even the "Door of the Displaced" had turned into a nearly transparent illusion, silently standing in its original position. Through that transparent door, Zhou Ming could see the last remaining part of the Homeloss—
A pitch-black wooden carved goat head floated there, hovering above the phantom of what used to be a chart table, turning its head to look at Alice and Zhou Ming standing not far away.
Zhou Ming walked towards the goat head, with an illusion of stars spread behind him, while the last structures of the Homeloss crumbled and vanished within that illusion.
"This is about it," he said to his first mate, "It’s time for the Homeloss to rest—Silantis is also waiting for you."
"Keep a spot for me on the new Homeloss in the new world," the goat head raised its neck, its stiff wooden face seemingly smiling, "You decide the format."
"Alright." Zhou Ming nodded.
The goat head exhaled softly, and after a moment of silence, it squinted its eyes and finally asked again that initial and ultimate question—
"Name?"
"Zhou Ming."
Brilliant starlight burst from the remaining structures of the Homeloss, silently engulfing the phantom of Saslouka’s spine and its skull, vanishing into the starlight in an instant, leaving only a few lingering dots of light slowly dissipating.
Alice’s eyes widened as she watched this scene, she raised her hand in the darkness as if to touch those drifting light dots, and when a spark fell on her fingertip, she seemed to realize belatedly, tried to smile, and vigorously waved her hand: "Goodbye, Mr. First Mate, goodbye—see you in the new world!"
The light dots disappeared, and the doll lady finally stopped waving her arms slowly, she pondered in the dark for a while, then looked up at Zhou Ming: "Captain, what’s next? Isn’t there... a little bit more way to go? I see the Black Sun still ahead, how do we get there?"
Zhou Ming smiled, reached out and patted Alice’s hair, raising his finger behind the doll.
Alice paused, then turned her head.
She saw a familiar, grand wooden box, silently floating in the darkness.
"I kept it separately, and now it’s up to you," Zhou Ming said next to her.
Alice finally realized, and then a happy smile appeared on her face.
She floated next to the wooden box, bent down and stroked the box, as if greeting an old friend, lightly caressing its surface: "Hello... we’re setting off again!"
Zhou Ming laughed and stepped into the wooden box, followed by Alice—the doll’s wooden box was not too big, just like a very small canoe, but still spacious enough for two people to stand.
Alice grabbed the floating wooden box lid nearby, but then hesitated a bit, looking uncertainly at Zhou Ming: "Captain, can we really row over? There’s no water here..."
But Zhou Ming just smiled, his gaze sweeping over the surrounding void and darkness, so in this exiled dimension obscured by the Creation of the World, the darkness began to ripple.
"It’s possible now," he said to the doll.
Alice blinked, tried to row with the lid in her hand through the surrounding darkness—the wooden box moved.
She suddenly became happy, beginning to vigorously wave the lid in her hand, rowing hard through the darkness—just like that first day, like when she chased after the disappearing Homeloss through the waves of the Endless Sea, the wooden box gradually accelerated through the darkness, carrying the doll and her captain towards the distant sunlight.
Time seemed to lose its meaning, the distance of space seemed to lose its meaning, the wooden box like a tiny canoe traveled through the crack of darkness towards the far sunlight, Alice didn’t know how long she had rowed, she only knew that the captain was always with her, and the distant sun always seemed to be at the same distance—suddenly, that sunlight reached a very close position, the distant sun became a sea of fire stretching out as far as the eye could see, right below the wooden box, huge fiery blasts surged like an amazing storm—yet silent and cold.
Alice stopped her movements, she peeked downward, then turned to look at Zhou Ming, a broad smile breaking across her face: "We’ve arrived!"
Zhou Ming remained silent for a long time, and after a while, he gently exhaled: "Yes, we’ve arrived."
Alice didn’t ask why the captain was silent for so long, she seemed to understand everything, after the captain’s reply, she solemnly placed the lid of the wooden box to one side, then raised her head to look into Zhou Ming’s eyes.
The brilliant smile gradually turned into a serene one.
"Captain, see you in the new world."
"Yes, see you in the new world."
"Don’t forget my little flat pan~"
"Of course—"
The doll contentedly vanished into the starlight.
Zhou Ming quietly stood in the sea of fire of the Black Sun, after a long while, he finally turned his head to look at his shoulder.
In the diffuse starlight, Ai Yi’s figure appeared intermittently.
It tilted its head, seemingly curiously observing its master—at the intersection of their gazes, it suddenly flapped its wings, emitting a strange, sharp, and seemingly interfered sound: "To the new world, to the new world, to the new world! New UR limited time UP, Duncan Zhouming probability enhancement! SSR card ’Alice’ limited reissue! To the new world! To the new world!"

chapters.title: Chapter 855 - 850: Depth 0, Assignment _3
chapters.content:
Chapter 855: Chapter 850: Depth 0, Assignment _3
Zhou Ming furrowed his brows in confusion.
Normally, the pigeon’s speech was abstract, but he could still understand it to some extent. But this time, it was a bit too abstract... What was this bird rambling about?
However, just as he was about to say something, the figure of Ai Yi had already begun to fade rapidly amidst the stars. It flapped its wings one last time, and those mung bean eyes that usually didn’t seem very bright suddenly appeared contemplative. Then, it turned its head and seemed to look seriously at its own owner.
"Good——bye——"
And then, the pigeon was gone.
Zhou Ming watched the scene in a daze for a while, shaking his head helplessly after a long time, muttering to himself, "I thought at least this guy would be with me till the end."
No one responded to his muttering.
Including the "sun" burning beneath his feet.
The Black Sun had "died". When Alice approached this sea of flames with the wooden box, Zhou Ming had noticed it.
Zhou Ming didn’t know when it had ceased its thought processes. Perhaps it was the moment the Homeloss entered the backside of Creation of the World, or maybe when Alice reached the sea of flames with her wooden box. During this process, the Black Sun had quietly stopped thinking; not saying goodbye, nor leaving any message.
Here remained a corpse still burning in accordance with a specific pattern, maintaining a beacon-like flash that could still illuminate the path after the apocalypse.
This flame was the last "gift" that Black Sun left for Zhou Ming.
"...You really trust in my promise."
Zhou Ming smiled helplessly and shook his head. His figure gradually descended above the sea of flames, until he was engulfed by the fire, until he felt himself standing on a solid surface.
And the flames that had once belonged to the Black Sun, now without an owner, were still burning fiercely by his side, as if waiting for... "usurpation".
Zhou Ming squinted his eyes, looking around the sea of flames, when suddenly... a word appeared in his mind.
Usurper.
And thus, the final Usurping Flame began.
In an instant, the residual flames of the Black Sun were transformed into carriers of starlight. This dazzling "celestial body", built up from twisted information and confused beliefs, was soaked in starlight as if ignited for the second time, and exploded rapidly, turning into a strong flash that illuminated everything here in an infinitely short moment.
The fierce "illumination" cast starlight into the fissures of Creation of the World—again, for an infinitely short moment.
After this instant, time truly lost its meaning.
The Black Sun, the last remnant of the old world, the final fragment left to this moment after the collision of countless worlds, was completely disintegrated in the starlight.
The Great Obliteration, completed.
...
All things vanished in the hollow echoes of the Great Obliteration, time and space turned into nullities, that nearly eternal yet infinitely brief "instant"... began.
Only one consciousness was floating in the void, walking through this eternal instant.
It began to think, and to calculate.
The mathematical machine’s first parameter was generated, and then, after an infinite length of time, the second parameter was cautiously determined—this process was too long to be measured, yet too short to be noticed.
It was still thinking, still calculating.
In the "time" that was infinitely long and short, it started the initial assignment for everything.
On an information scale that was both calculable and incalculable, it began arranging deserved promises into their rightful places.
It was still thinking, still calculating.
It began to decide the node for the operation of all things; in this yet-to-start mathematical machine, what came before the node belonged to "design", what followed belonged to the "future of possibilities".
This process took another infinitely long instant.
...
Invoke.
From the old world - assignment - completed.
Redirection done.
To the new world - model has been injected.
Thus, the eternal first second passed.
Zhou Ming-Duncan opened his eyes.
The void’s darkness reflected in his eyes.
...
He said—
"Let there be light."

chapters.title: Chapter 856 - 851: Depth, -1 — To the New World
chapters.content:
Chapter 856: Chapter 851: Depth, -1 — To the New World
And then, there was light.
But that was a long, long time ago—or it could have been just a moment ago.
After all, if the Astrologers of Algraid are correct, the birth of this universe might have just happened not long ago—although for the time scale of all beings in the universe, it may have been "billions of years ago". Yet, for another time scale that transcends all things in the universe, billions of years are merely an insignificant parameter.
But who cares? At any rate, a senior student, who is busy completing their biology thesis and whose daily sleep has been reduced to less than six hours, definitely won’t care about these "heavenly matters"—the next-door astronomy club might care, but that’s a different story, their credits are tied to this.
Borno, clutching a stack of materials just borrowed from the library, hurried across the top walkway of the college city, his pace brisk as if stirring up a gust of wind.
He ran past an Elf gentleman with messy hair and seemingly severely lacking sleep, nearly colliding with him.
"No running on the upper walkways!" The Elf gentleman with messy hair stumbled a bit, loudly reminding the short youngster who seemed to appear out of nowhere—judging by his small stature and distinct feline-like ears, he must be a Jipulo student, this race is always so reckless.
"I’m sorry, sir!" Borno hastily stopped, turned around, and bowed deeply, almost throwing the stack of books in his arms onto the gentleman, "I’m in a hurry to meet my mentor—I stayed in the library too long, and when I looked at the clock, I realized I was almost half an hour late! I’m terribly sorry, did I hurt you?"
The sincere and anxious attitude of the Jipulo lad had its effect, and the Elf gentleman waved his hand somewhat helplessly: "Alright, go on then, but don’t miss your mentor’s appointment—it’s no small matter. Just don’t dash around like that again, the world won’t end because you’re a bit slower."
"Yes... Thank you, sir! Goodbye, sir! I’m leaving, sir!"
Borno kept bowing repeatedly, and then clumsily caught the books slipping from his embrace, before turning and quickly walking towards the other end of the walkway.
The Elf man with messy hair and dark circles from lack of sleep shook his head helplessly as he watched the young man dash away clumsily.
Footsteps came from beside him, he looked up in the direction of the sound, and saw a familiar figure that had already approached. A smile appeared on his face, and he greeted the person, "Ted, it’s rare to see you free for a walk at this time."
"It’s even rarer to see you willing to leave your lab and breathe the outside air," Ted Riel glanced at the Elf scholar in front of him and casually joked, "Didn’t you say that Elves only need to absorb basic nutrients and maintain 15 minutes of sunlight exposure and two minutes of outdoor activity each day to sustain their life signs?"
"I do think so—but my doctor thinks otherwise," Taran El shrugged, "He kicked me out of the lab."
"...Good riddance," Ted Riel rolled his eyes, "Your body would die young before reaching 2000 years old if no one watched over you—seriously, the world is beautiful, don’t you want to live a few more years, see the world thoroughly before dying? Must you be so stubborn?"
Hearing his long-time good friend’s unabashed teasing and lecturing, Taran El just chuckled sheepishly, unable to retort, and touched his nose.
"Yes... It’s so nice..."
He muttered softly, then slowly raised his head, looking towards the end of the walkway. His gaze passed over the spire of the college tower, beyond the high walls, over the vast plains and hills outside the city, and towards the horizon.
There were magnificent, mountain-like greens undulating across the land, immense tree shadows stood at the horizon’s edge, and the pale green magical lights emanating from the top of those canopies spread across the sky like auroras, forming a river of light flowing towards the plains. The greenery flowed like veins in the earth, some on the surface and some seeping underground, disappearing at certain tributaries’ ends.
The energy streams known as "Saslouka’s Touch" penetrated deeply into the ground and intertwined into an even larger network near the mantle, enveloping the entire planet between the crust and the mantle—wherever the energy streams reached, it was a place blessed by Silantis.
This "college city" was built upon the largest energy focus on the gentle wind plains.
But in reality, these "energy foci" serve little purpose for the city itself—it’s electricity and fuel that the city needs for operation. The only use of these deep underground energy foci is to allow Elves to establish more direct communication with Silantis.
Silantis likes talking to people—Saslouka does too, She too would go online during Her patrols.
Taran El squinted, bright sunlight beaming on his face, bringing a warmth that made one irresistibly sleepy.
"Did you hear about that?" Ted Riel’s voice came from beside, waking Taran El from his drowsiness, "The Astrologers of Algraid—they found out about some serious situations."
"...There’s always all sorts of information flowing from the borderlands, and Terra has long-term stable exchanges with the borderlands, moreover... The people of Algraid have always been highly sensitive to the stars," Taran El spoke unhurriedly, "I think it’s not a big deal—if the world is such, then it should be as it is; since they have noticed, let them know, after all... there are so many equally sensitive and intelligent races living in such a vast cosmic expanse, and what we can reach and influence is always only the smallest part of it..."
The scholar said, stretching lazily in the sunlight as if he was trying to draw the sunlight into his lungs, then slowly exhaled.
"Ted, don’t think too much, enjoy the air and breeze like I do, and the warm sunlight... Honestly, I’m really starting to like being outdoors, turns out basking in the sun is quite a pleasant thing."
Ted Riel glanced at Taran, then similarly seemed to relax all of a sudden, smiling and shaking his head as he, too, squinted his eyes to let the warm sunshine touch his face.
But just after a moment, he suddenly seemed to recall something, and couldn’t help but mutter softly: "That being said, how do you think ’he’ would view this? Among the stars, native intelligent beings are beginning to spontaneously perceive some of the mysteries in the birth process of this world..."
Taran El shrugged: "Him? He doesn’t really have an opinion."
"...How do you know?"
"Lady Lucresia told me when she came back last time—’He’ now has a lot on his plate, and as for the various circumstances emerging among the native intelligent beings in the stars... ’He’ follows one principle: as long as they don’t tear down the house, he does not intervene."
"...Is that a bit too lenient?"
"Who knows?" Taran El casually remarked, "How does that saying go again... Oh, to ensure the ’possibilities’ that this world possesses to the greatest extent possible, probably something like that."
Ted Riel thought for a moment, felt there was profound and compelling logic in it, and decided not to dwell on this topic anymore, but just curiously asked: "Do you know what ’he’ is busy with right now?"
"Then I know even less, but... such a vast place, he definitely has a lot to attend to."
As Taran El spoke, he looked up at the distant sky.
He seemed to gaze at a place infinitely far away—beyond planets, beyond galaxies, in the crevices of space-time ripples, in some endless spatial structure depth that surpasses human understanding.
He had only briefly revisited that place a few times through guided illusions.
Visited that ship.
The place in the oldest and most obscure Barbosan legends where the "Ancient Spirits" gather—
...
"The situation is this," the tall Fenna stood up—in some deep-space tales, she is also referred to as "Sword-wielding Saintess," or "Star Feller," "Lady of the Falling Stars"—and said sternly, "It’s a bit tricky; we might have to go there ourselves."
The imposing figure at the end of the long table remained silent, and across the table, Sherry had already laid her head down on her arms—she had been known by Barbosans as the "Lady Surveying the Skies" or "Star Thrower" from some time ago: "But I just went on vacation yesterday!"
"We still have to save them," said Agatha (Shadow) sitting in the corner of the long table, shaking her head, "if only because they are also part of the crew..."
"Just don’t let this get out," Morris, with his pipe in his mouth, glanced at the tall figure at the end of the table—his titles were so numerous that sometimes even he couldn’t remember them all—said with a subtly complex expression, "Especially not to the Leviathans; they’ve already protested three times..."
The towering figure at the end of the table finally stirred, and thus the voices around the table calmed down slightly.
All eyes laden with expectation fell on the captain.
That figure rose from the darkness—Duncan Zhouming scanned his followers gathered here, and after a long and complex silence, he finally sighed, his expression increasingly frantic:
"So, who can first explain, ’During the trip, Lei Nora decoyed the Leviathan queen who had sneaked out to admire the cosmic spectacle, and they both ended up trapped in a spatial crack due to gravity collapse, having to send a distress signal for help to pull them out’—and then briefly explain why this is the fourth time?! What happened the previous three times?!"
At that moment, Nina raised her head cautiously looking around, murmuring: "Shouldn’t we first explain what the cosmic spectacle is? It sounds interesting..."
Just as Nina’s words fell, the goat head on the table suddenly lifted its neck, its tone very excited: "Hey, I know this, I saw it during the last patrol mission, it’s like when a quasar encounters..."
Before it could finish, everyone around the table shouted in unison: "Shut up!"
"...Oh."
(Grand Finale)
(Indeed, the depth 0 of the previous Chapter was the grand finale of the deep sea era, but even though the era of the deep sea has ended, their story continues, so—
Depth -1
Homeloss is still voyaging.)
